   - development-side parallelization now
   - harness-in-action parallelization later

1	Date: 2026-04-22
2	Status: proposed integrated program plan
3	
4	# Harness Modifier Development Program Plan
5	
6	## Role
7	
8	- [g:r:i] This artifact is the current integrated plan for developing the harness-modifier program itself.
9	- [g:r:i] It is not a host-product roadmap, not a Phase 01 relaunch plan, and not a claim that the modifier is ready for broad deployment.
10	- [d:r:i] Its job is to gather the current active pressures into one bounded program object:
11	  - responsible closure
12	  - development-side parallelization
13	  - intervention lifecycle review / monitor / iterate discipline
14	  - extraction/deployability sequencing
15	  - actual and possible intervention surfaces
16	  - horizon routing
17	  - task-type routing
18	
19	## Scope Rule
20	
21	- [g:r:i] Harness-program horizons are separate from `prix-guesser` product horizons.
22	- [g:r:i] Development-side parallelization for the harness-modifier program is the active protocol question now.
23	- [d:r:i] Harness-in-action parallelization remains a real later family, but it is not the current implementation target for this plan.
24	- [d:r:i] When this plan says `uplift`, it refers to the harness-modifier program unless it names another target explicitly.
25	
26	## Domain Split
27	
28	- [d:r:i] This plan routes through the currently explicit uplift target split:
29	  - `harness-contract`
30	  - `host-artifact`
31	  - `harness-agential`
32	  - `harness-operational`
33	  - `harness-adaptive`
34	  - `distribution/deployability`
35	- [d:r:i] The active program problem is not just contract improvement. It is the combined improvement of:
36	  - the modifier as a portable contract surface
37	  - the modifier as an agential project-development machine
38	  - the modifier as a future deployable/distributable system
39	
40	## Actual Intervention Surfaces
41	
42	- [d:r:i] The current actual intervention surfaces for developing the harness-modifier are:
43	  - `audit / review lane machinery`
44	    - lane packets, specs, prompts, launch truth, outputs, dispositions, timing ledgers
45	  - `governance routing`
46	    - `CURRENT-STATE.md`
47	    - `STATUS.md`
48	    - `INDEX.md`
49	    - `.planning/HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md`
50	    - `AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md`
51	    - `.planning/AGENTS.md`
52	    - `WORKFLOW.md`
53	    - readiness compaction prompts
54	  - `propagation carry`
55	    - change-triggered refresh notes
56	    - propagation baseline/delta carriers
57	    - propagation-review route
58	  - `verification and materialization`
59	    - tests
60	    - installer/materialization checks
61	    - parity carriers
62	    - contract verification
63	  - `extraction / rehome work`
64	    - `harness_modifier/` carrier moves
65	    - overlay authority splits
66	    - helper neutralization
67	    - payload-home judgment
68	  - `responsible-closure field mapping`
69	    - deployability
70	    - host-context testing breadth
71	    - adaptive feedback
72	    - discrepancy and positive-gain capture
73	    - agential closure quality
74	  - `development-overlap governance`
75	    - safe companion work
76	    - waiting / recheck discipline
77	    - delegation boundaries
78	
79	## Possible Or Virtual Intervention Surfaces
80	
81	- [g:r:i] The program should not map only already-materialized surfaces. It should also keep openable surfaces visible when repeated pressure suggests they may need to exist.
82	- [d:r:i] The current possible or virtual intervention surfaces are:
83	  - `development parallelization protocol carrier`
84	    - a canonical protocol for lane-local read-set, companion work, must-wait surfaces, recheck timing, and same-basis concurrency
85	  - `intervention lifecycle protocol carrier`
86	    - propose -> launch -> monitor -> review -> disposition -> propagate -> verify -> revise
87	  - `single-writer / lane-exclusive authority surface map`
88	    - broader than governance files alone
89	  - `fan-out packet template`
90	    - for safe concurrent readers over a frozen basis
91	  - `parallelization impact carrier` inside propagation review
92	  - `development intervention-surface map`
93	    - a dedicated map of actual and virtual surfaces for developing the modifier
94	  - `measurement/provenance carrier`
95	    - explicit capture of lane-side observations, discrepancies, positive gains, and provenance
96	  - `observation carrier` for host exercises
97	  - `dogfooding surface`
98	    - a later possibility where the modifier is developed in its own repo and can use itself more directly
99	- [d:r:i] A virtual surface is worth promoting only when:
100	  - repeated pressure appears across more than one family
101	  - current carriers cannot hold the needed distinction cleanly
102	  - ownership can be made explicit if the surface is created
103	  - propagation consequences can be named in advance
104	  - the surface can be audited or verified once opened
105	
106	## Planning Stance
107	
108	- [g:r:i] The active stance is `responsible closure`, not `rush to deployment`.
109	- [g:r:i] The goal is not to stop widening. The goal is to widen in a way that prepares the modifier for real deployment, adaptation, and later repo separation without blurring program governance.
110	- [d:r:i] The current program should therefore prioritize:
111	  - stronger protocol and lifecycle discipline for development
112	  - stronger visibility of actual and possible intervention surfaces
113	  - stronger responsible-closure sequencing
114	  - explicit later boundaries where the field is not yet earned
115	
116	## Short Horizon
117	
118	- [d:r:i] `audit`
119	  - freeze responsible-closure lane `01` as a completed baseline
120	  - preserve the paired internal parallelization cross-audit as a durable inheritance note
121	  - run a cross-vendor audit over this plan
122	- [d:r:i] `planning / protocol`
123	  - cut one bounded development-parallelization protocol tranche
124	  - cut one bounded intervention lifecycle protocol tranche
125	  - make lane-local companion-work / must-wait / recheck rules explicit
126	- [d:r:i] `audit / propagation`
127	  - run a targeted propagation audit on already-landed parallelization-adjacent workflow changes
128	  - preserve external-lane measurement/provenance implications rather than leaving them ownerless
129	- [d:r:i] `governance`
130	  - route the plan into the live governing surfaces
131	  - keep harness-program horizons distinct from host-product horizons
132	
133	## Medium Horizon
134	
135	- [d:r:i] `planning / implementation`
136	  - close `160` payload-home judgment on the cleaner program baseline
137	  - open the first development intervention-surface map if `166` still proves too compact to carry the field alone
138	- [d:r:i] `planning / research`
139	  - cut the first durable observation-carrier proposal for deployability/adaptive feedback
140	  - define the first actual host-exercise packet for observe-only dry-run work
141	- [d:r:i] `audit / verification`
142	  - run one observe-only second-host dry run
143	  - run one observe-only mixed `.codex` + held-annotation `.claude` dry run if earned
144	- [d:r:i] `protocol`
145	  - decide whether the virtual surfaces above should remain virtual, become proposals, or become real carriers
146	
147	## Long Horizon
148	
149	- [d:r:i] `research / planning`
150	  - standalone harness-modifier repo
151	  - npm / `npx` distribution
152	  - stronger dogfooding posture once repo separation exists
153	- [d:r:i] `adaptive`
154	  - richer telemetry and semantic-signal capture
155	  - stronger discrepancy / positive-gain sedimentation
156	  - post-deploy correction loops
157	- [d:r:i] `parallelization in action`
158	  - workflow-local harness parallelization beyond current execution-wave patterns
159	  - only after development-side protocol work and closure discipline are stronger
160	
161	## Task-Type Routing
162	
163	- [d:r:i] `exploration`
164	  - virtual intervention surface discovery
165	  - dogfooding posture
166	  - future workflow/skill/template openings
167	- [d:r:i] `audit`
168	  - cross-vendor plan review
169	  - targeted propagation audits
170	  - responsible-closure rereads
171	  - later harness-in-action parallelization diagnosis
172	- [d:r:i] `research`
173	  - GSD / GSD Reflect reference-field comparison for telemetry and lifecycle ideas
174	  - deployment-context and host-exercise field shaping
175	- [d:r:i] `planning`
176	  - protocol carriers
177	  - lifecycle carriers
178	  - observation carriers
179	  - second-host exercise plans
180	- [d:r:i] `implementation`
181	  - protocol surfaces once plan/audit clears them
182	  - payload-home closure
183	  - later observation carrier
184	- [d:r:i] `verification`
185	  - tests
186	  - installer/materialization checks
187	  - host observe-only dry runs
188	  - propagation refresh validation
189	- [d:r:i] `governance`
190	  - current-state / status / register / index routing
191	  - launch-truth and ledger upkeep
192	  - continuity prompt carry
193	
194	## Workstreams
195	
196	- [d:r:i] `Workstream A: development operations and protocol`
197	  - current status: under-carried
198	  - next type: planning -> audit -> implementation
199	  - main objects: development parallelization protocol, intervention lifecycle protocol, lane-local overlap rules
200	- [d:r:i] `Workstream B: responsible closure and deployability`
201	  - current status: first field map completed
202	  - next type: planning -> audit -> implementation
203	  - main objects: payload-home judgment, observation carrier, host-context dry-run exercises
204	- [d:r:i] `Workstream C: propagation and verification`
205	  - current status: strong field map exists, but parallelization-adjacent consequences are still unevenly carried
206	  - next type: audit -> propagation refresh -> governance
207	  - main objects: targeted propagation audit over already-landed workflow changes, later `Parallelization Impact` extension if earned
208	- [d:r:i] `Workstream D: intervention-surface expansion`
209	  - current status: actual surfaces are partly visible, virtual surfaces are not yet governed strongly enough
210	  - next type: exploration -> planning
211	  - main objects: actual/virtual development intervention-surface map, criteria for promoting virtual surfaces
212	
213	## Parallelization Rule
214	
215	- [g:r:i] The current plan uses parallelization first as a development-program multiplier, not as a harness-in-action rewrite agenda.
216	- [d:r:i] Safe overlap for this plan:
217	  - external plan audit lane plus unrelated governance carry
218	  - later paired internal audit plus parent-thread plan revision
219	  - later targeted propagation audit on already-landed workflow slices while another bounded read-only audit is in flight
220	- [d:r:i] Out of scope for this plan:
221	  - harness-in-action workflow rewrites
222	  - execute-family or review-family redesigns
223	  - broad multi-provider portability
224	
225	## Responsible Closure Rule
226	
227	- [g:r:i] Responsible closure for this program means stronger control, better routing, cleaner maintainability, and better adaptive capacity, not just more proof that the current modifier can run.
228	- [d:r:i] The plan should therefore be judged by whether it:
229	  - exposes actual and possible intervention surfaces
230	  - keeps horizons explicit
231	  - keeps task types explicit
232	  - sequences closure and deployability without rush pressure
233	  - preserves later futures instead of foreclosing them through local convenience
234	
235	## Exact Next Moves
236	
237	1. [d:r:i] Treat this plan as the active integrated development-program object.
238	2. [d:r:i] Audit this plan cross-vendor before cutting the next protocol tranche.
239	3. [d:r:i] After that audit returns, land one bounded development-parallelization and intervention-lifecycle protocol slice.
240	4. [d:r:i] Pair that protocol slice with one targeted propagation audit over already-landed parallelization-adjacent workflow changes.
241	5. [d:r:i] Return next to `160` payload-home judgment and the responsible-closure deployability bundle from the cleaner protocol baseline.
242	6. [d:r:i] Keep harness-in-action parallelization explicit, but later.
243

- [d:r:i] Its job is to gather the current active pressures into one bounded program object:
  - responsible closure
  - development-side parallelization
  - intervention lifecycle review / monitor / iterate discipline
  - extraction/deployability sequencing
  - actual and possible intervention surfaces
  - horizon routing
  - task-type routing

## Scope Rule

- [g:r:i] Harness-program horizons are separate from `prix-guesser` product horizons.
- [g:r:i] Development-side parallelization for the harness-modifier program is the active protocol question now.
- [d:r:i] Harness-in-action parallelization remains a real later family, but it is not the current implementation target for this plan.
- [d:r:i] When this plan says `uplift`, it refers to the harness-modifier program unless it names another target explicitly.

## Domain Split

- [d:r:i] This plan routes through the currently explicit uplift target split:
  - `harness-contract`
  - `host-artifact`
  - `harness-agential`
  - `harness-operational`
  - `harness-adaptive`
  - `distribution/deployability`
- [d:r:i] The active program problem is not just contract improvement. It is the combined improvement of:
  - the modifier as a portable contract surface
  - the modifier as an agential project-development machine
  - the modifier as a future deployable/distributable system

## Actual Intervention Surfaces

- [d:r:i] The current actual intervention surfaces for developing the harness-modifier are:
  - `audit / review lane machinery`
    - lane packets, specs, prompts, launch truth, outputs, dispositions, timing ledgers
  - `governance routing`
    - `CURRENT-STATE.md`
    - `STATUS.md`
    - `INDEX.md`
    - `.planning/HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md`
    - `AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md`
    - `.planning/AGENTS.md`
    - `WORKFLOW.md`
    - readiness compaction prompts
  - `propagation carry`
    - change-triggered refresh notes
    - propagation baseline/delta carriers
    - propagation-review route
  - `verification and materialization`
    - tests
    - installer/materialization checks
    - parity carriers
    - contract verification
  - `extraction / rehome work`
    - `harness_modifier/` carrier moves
    - overlay authority splits
    - helper neutralization
    - payload-home judgment
  - `responsible-closure field mapping`
    - deployability
    - host-context testing breadth
    - adaptive feedback
    - discrepancy and positive-gain capture
    - agential closure quality
  - `development-overlap governance`
    - safe companion work
    - waiting / recheck discipline
    - delegation boundaries

## Possible Or Virtual Intervention Surfaces

- [g:r:i] The program should not map only already-materialized surfaces. It should also keep openable surfaces visible when repeated pressure suggests they may need to exist.
- [d:r:i] The current possible or virtual intervention surfaces are:
  - `development parallelization protocol carrier`
    - a canonical protocol for lane-local read-set, companion work, must-wait surfaces, recheck timing, and same-basis concurrency
  - `intervention lifecycle protocol carrier`
    - propose -> launch -> monitor -> review -> disposition -> propagate -> verify -> revise
  - `single-writer / lane-exclusive authority surface map`
    - broader than governance files alone
  - `fan-out packet template`
    - for safe concurrent readers over a frozen basis
  - `parallelization impact carrier` inside propagation review
  - `development intervention-surface map`
    - a dedicated map of actual and virtual surfaces for developing the modifier
  - `measurement/provenance carrier`
    - explicit capture of lane-side observations, discrepancies, positive gains, and provenance
  - `observation carrier` for host exercises
  - `dogfooding surface`
    - a later possibility where the modifier is developed in its own repo and can use itself more directly
- [d:r:i] A virtual surface is worth promoting only when:
  - repeated pressure appears across more than one family
  - current carriers cannot hold the needed distinction cleanly
  - ownership can be made explicit if the surface is created
  - propagation consequences can be named in advance
  - the surface can be audited or verified once opened

## Planning Stance

- [g:r:i] The active stance is `responsible closure`, not `rush to deployment`.
- [g:r:i] The goal is not to stop widening. The goal is to widen in a way that prepares the modifier for real deployment, adaptation, and later repo separation without blurring program governance.
- [d:r:i] The current program should therefore prioritize:
  - stronger protocol and lifecycle discipline for development
  - stronger visibility of actual and possible intervention surfaces
  - stronger responsible-closure sequencing
  - explicit later boundaries where the field is not yet earned

## Short Horizon

- [d:r:i] `audit`
  - freeze responsible-closure lane `01` as a completed baseline
  - preserve the paired internal parallelization cross-audit as a durable inheritance note
  - run a cross-vendor audit over this plan
- [d:r:i] `planning / protocol`
  - cut one bounded development-parallelization protocol tranche
  - cut one bounded intervention lifecycle protocol tranche
  - make lane-local companion-work / must-wait / recheck rules explicit
- [d:r:i] `audit / propagation`
  - run a targeted propagation audit on already-landed parallelization-adjacent workflow changes
  - preserve external-lane measurement/provenance implications rather than leaving them ownerless
- [d:r:i] `governance`
  - route the plan into the live governing surfaces
  - keep harness-program horizons distinct from host-product horizons

## Medium Horizon

- [d:r:i] `planning / implementation`
  - close `160` payload-home judgment on the cleaner program baseline
  - open the first development intervention-surface map if `166` still proves too compact to carry the field alone
- [d:r:i] `planning / research`
  - cut the first durable observation-carrier proposal for deployability/adaptive feedback
  - define the first actual host-exercise packet for observe-only dry-run work
- [d:r:i] `audit / verification`
  - run one observe-only second-host dry run
  - run one observe-only mixed `.codex` + held-annotation `.claude` dry run if earned
- [d:r:i] `protocol`
  - decide whether the virtual surfaces above should remain virtual, become proposals, or become real carriers

## Long Horizon

- [d:r:i] `research / planning`
  - standalone harness-modifier repo
  - npm / `npx` distribution
  - stronger dogfooding posture once repo separation exists
- [d:r:i] `adaptive`
  - richer telemetry and semantic-signal capture
  - stronger discrepancy / positive-gain sedimentation
  - post-deploy correction loops
- [d:r:i] `parallelization in action`
  - workflow-local harness parallelization beyond current execution-wave patterns
  - only after development-side protocol work and closure discipline are stronger

## Task-Type Routing

- [d:r:i] `exploration`
  - virtual intervention surface discovery
  - dogfooding posture
  - future workflow/skill/template openings
- [d:r:i] `audit`
  - cross-vendor plan review
  - targeted propagation audits
  - responsible-closure rereads
  - later harness-in-action parallelization diagnosis
- [d:r:i] `research`
  - GSD / GSD Reflect reference-field comparison for telemetry and lifecycle ideas
  - deployment-context and host-exercise field shaping
- [d:r:i] `planning`
  - protocol carriers
  - lifecycle carriers
  - observation carriers
  - second-host exercise plans
- [d:r:i] `implementation`
  - protocol surfaces once plan/audit clears them
  - payload-home closure
  - later observation carrier
- [d:r:i] `verification`
  - tests
  - installer/materialization checks
  - host observe-only dry runs
  - propagation refresh validation
- [d:r:i] `governance`
  - current-state / status / register / index routing
  - launch-truth and ledger upkeep
  - continuity prompt carry

## Workstreams

- [d:r:i] `Workstream A: development operations and protocol`
  - current status: under-carried
  - next type: planning -> audit -> implementation
  - main objects: development parallelization protocol, intervention lifecycle protocol, lane-local overlap rules
- [d:r:i] `Workstream B: responsible closure and deployability`
  - current status: first field map completed
  - next type: planning -> audit -> implementation
  - main objects: payload-home judgment, observation carrier, host-context dry-run exercises
- [d:r:i] `Workstream C: propagation and verification`
  - current status: strong field map exists, but parallelization-adjacent consequences are still unevenly carried
  - next type: audit -> propagation refresh -> governance
  - main objects: targeted propagation audit over already-landed workflow changes, later `Parallelization Impact` extension if earned
- [d:r:i] `Workstream D: intervention-surface expansion`
  - current status: actual surfaces are partly visible, virtual surfaces are not yet governed strongly enough
  - next type: exploration -> planning
  - main objects: actual/virtual development intervention-surface map, criteria for promoting virtual surfaces

## Parallelization Rule

- [g:r:i] The current plan uses parallelization first as a development-program multiplier, not as a harness-in-action rewrite agenda.
- [d:r:i] Safe overlap for this plan:
  - external plan audit lane plus unrelated governance carry
  - later paired internal audit plus parent-thread plan revision
  - later targeted propagation audit on already-landed workflow slices while another bounded read-only audit is in flight
- [d:r:i] Out of scope for this plan:
  - harness-in-action workflow rewrites
  - execute-family or review-family redesigns
  - broad multi-provider portability

## Responsible Closure Rule

- [g:r:i] Responsible closure for this program means stronger control, better routing, cleaner maintainability, and better adaptive capacity, not just more proof that the current modifier can run.
- [d:r:i] The plan should therefore be judged by whether it:
  - exposes actual and possible intervention surfaces
  - keeps horizons explicit
  - keeps task types explicit
  - sequences closure and deployability without rush pressure
  - preserves later futures instead of foreclosing them through local convenience

## Exact Next Moves

1. [d:r:i] Treat this plan as the active integrated development-program object.
2. [d:r:i] Audit this plan cross-vendor before cutting the next protocol tranche.
3. [d:r:i] After that audit returns, land one bounded development-parallelization and intervention-lifecycle protocol slice.
4. [d:r:i] Pair that protocol slice with one targeted propagation audit over already-landed parallelization-adjacent workflow changes.
5. [d:r:i] Return next to `160` payload-home judgment and the responsible-closure deployability bundle from the cleaner protocol baseline.
6. [d:r:i] Keep harness-in-action parallelization explicit, but later.

# Harness Modifier Responsible Closure, Deployability, And Adaptive Feedback Route

## Role

- [d:r:i] This route note makes responsible closure explicit without turning it into rush pressure.
- [d:r:i] Its job is to keep deployability, testing breadth, post-deploy learning, telemetry/feedback shape, and adaptive follow-through visible as an active harness-improvement family while the current extraction and propagation work continues.

## Why This Route Is Active Now

- [d:r:i] The modifier is no longer only a local experiment inside one repo. It is now being shaped toward later standalone travel, installability, and reuse across host projects with `.codex`, `.claude`, or both.
- [d:r:i] That means closure pressure is no longer only:
  - extraction cleanliness
  - propagation carry
  - compatibility disclosure
- [d:r:i] It also now includes:
  - deployability
  - host-context testing breadth
  - feedback/measurement/telemetry
  - discrepancy capture when behavior diverges from expectation
  - online adaptation and sedimentation of improved doctrine or contracts

## Route Commitments

### 1. Deployability Without Premature Closure

- [d:r:i] Aim toward a deployable modifier soon, but do not let `deployable soon` flatten stronger extraction, propagation, or maintainability work into rush pressure.
- [d:r:i] Treat responsible closure as:
  - cleaner authority
  - explicit compatibility
  - stronger testing
  - better post-deploy observability
  - better correction surfaces
  rather than as a finish-line declaration.

### 2. Harness-Agential Uplift

- [d:r:i] Responsible closure is not only about cleaner contracts and deployment posture.
- [d:r:i] It is also about the harness as a software-development / project machine:
  - handling multiple horizons more clearly
  - preserving promising later futures without blur
  - adapting under new external pressure without quietly shrinking ambition
  - revising specifics without losing the larger orienting project
- [d:r:i] That means closure work should also improve:
  - horizon-routing clarity
  - deferred/open finding governance
  - future-preservation doctrine
  - how later audits and reviews re-shape the program without semantic confusion

### 3. Adaptive Feedback And Telemetry

- [d:r:i] The modifier should gain explicit carriers for:
  - deployment context
  - observed behavior versus expected behavior
  - discrepancy or deviation recording
  - positive gain capture, not only breakage capture
  - richer semantic signal families rather than only counts
- [d:r:i] The measurement layer should not collapse into:
  - pass/fail defect tallies
  - one scalar success metric
  - binary positive/negative framing
- [d:r:i] It should widen what can later be interpreted, compared, and acted on.

### 4. Testing Breadth Across Host Contexts

- [d:r:i] The target field is not `all providers`.
- [d:r:i] The target field is:
  - `.codex` host
  - `.claude` host
  - mixed `.codex` + `.claude` host
  - hosts using regular get-shit-done
  - hosts carrying pre-existing get-shit-done-reflect artifacts that need uplift, translation, or explicit coexistence handling even though the modifier itself targets regular get-shit-done

### 5. Parallelization And Throughput

- [d:r:i] Responsible closure should not assume throughput only improves by shortening work.
- [d:r:i] It should also ask where overlap or sub-agent splitting is earned without degrading quality:
  - during harness-modifier development
  - during harness operation itself
  - across lateral workflow families beyond `execute-phase`
- [d:r:i] The task is not generic appetite for more parallel work.
- [d:r:i] The task is to design better overlap and partitioning protocols so more uplift can travel in the same wall-clock time without coherence loss.

### 6. Later Cross-Vendor Challenge

- [d:r:i] A bounded cross-vendor `responsible closure` audit is earned later.
- [d:r:i] That lane should challenge:
  - deployability readiness
  - harness-agential uplift quality
  - measurement/feedback route quality
  - adaptive post-deploy learning design
  - parallelization / throughput design
  - administrative/governance upkeep
  - maintainability under continued uplift
  - what is still being neglected relative to stronger closure
- [d:r:i] That audit should be opened after the current extraction/payload-home boundary settles a little farther, not as a vague ambient future wish.

## Reference Field

- [d:r:i] `get-shit-done-reflect` remains a useful reference field for measurement, signal capture, lifecycle, and ontology work, especially:
  - [~/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/CHANGELOG.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/CHANGELOG.md)
  - [~/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/.planning/audits/2026-04-15-measurement-signal-inventory/pre-57.5-handoff.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/.planning/audits/2026-04-15-measurement-signal-inventory/pre-57.5-handoff.md)
- [d:r:i] Use that repo as a reference field, not as the ceiling. The modifier should absorb what is valuable there while still trying to carry cleaner deployability, clearer propagation, stronger adaptive feedback, and better maintainability.

## Near Route

1. [d:r:i] Finish the current extraction/payload-home boundary cleanly.
2. [d:r:i] Freeze the semantic split around uplift targets/modes, harness-program horizons, and parallelization opportunity mapping so deployability work does not inherit blurred scope.

4. [d:r:i] Use that field map to define one first slice around feedback/measurement/telemetry carriers and one first slice around deployment/testing breadth.
5. [d:r:i] Then run the later cross-vendor responsible-closure audit against that more explicit bundle.

4	# Harness Uplift Semantics And Target-Mode Split
5	
6	## Role
7	
8	- [d:r:i] This note fixes a recurring semantic blur around the word `uplift`.
9	- [d:r:i] Its job is to distinguish what is being uplifted, in what sense, and by what mode, so later extraction, deployability, host-artifact, and harness-agential work do not get misread as one flattened family.
10	
11	## Why This Note Exists
12	
13	- [d:r:i] The workspace currently contains three overlapping projects:
14	  - the `prix-guesser` host product
15	  - the repo-local harness-modifier development program
16	  - the later standalone/distributable harness-modifier project
17	- [d:r:i] When those are not kept distinct, host-product horizon carriers can be over-read as harness-program horizon carriers, and host-artifact uplift can be misread as harness-agential improvement.
18	
19	## Uplift Targets
20	
21	### 1. Harness-Contract Uplift
22	
23	- [d:r:i] The target is the harness as a contract-bearing system:
24	  - workflows
25	  - skills
26	  - registries
27	  - helper boundaries
28	  - installer/materialization logic
29	  - propagation routes
30	  - review routes
31	  - extraction seams
32	
33	### 2. Host-Artifact Uplift
34	
35	- [d:r:i] The target is the host repo's existing operational corpus:
36	  - `.planning/STATE.md`
37	  - `.planning/phases/*`
38	  - uplift memory
39	  - runtime directories
40	  - seed corpora
41	  - migration packets
42	- [d:r:i] This is the family that keeps a host repo runnable or more readable under the modified harness.
43	
44	### 3. Harness-Agential Uplift
45	
46	- [d:r:i] The target is the harness as a software-development / project / planning machine.
47	- [d:r:i] This includes:
48	  - handling multiple horizons without blur
49	  - adapting to new evidence without drift
50	  - preserving promising futures without premature closure
51	  - routing deferred/open findings more cleanly
52	  - carrying long-horizon orientation while remaining revisable
53	
54	### 4. Harness-Operational Uplift
55	
56	- [d:r:i] The target is the improvement program's own execution posture:
57	  - launch truth
58	  - inheritance/disposition
59	  - timing calibration
60	  - overlap discipline
61	  - sub-agent onboarding and continuity
62	  - governance/admin carry while lanes run
63	
64	### 5. Harness-Adaptive Uplift
65	
66	- [d:r:i] The target is post-deploy learning and correction:
67	  - discrepancy capture
68	  - semantic signal capture
69	  - expectation-versus-observation comparison
70	  - doctrine sedimentation
71	  - adaptive correction loops
72	
73	### 6. Distribution / Deployability Uplift
74	
75	- [d:r:i] The target is travel across host repos and runtimes:
76	  - extraction into its own repo
77	  - installability
78	  - compatibility declaration
79	  - host-context testing breadth
80	  - deployment and upgrade surfaces
81	
82	## Uplift Modes
83	
84	- [d:r:i] `neutralize`
85	  - remove host-local or helper-local literals so a cleaner carrier can own them
86	- [d:r:i] `externalize`
87	  - move a contract, policy, or grammar into a named carrier
88	- [d:r:i] `propagate`
89	  - carry a changed contract through its neighboring producer / consumer / registry / governance surfaces
90	- [d:r:i] `classify`
91	  - distinguish cases that should not yet be collapsed into one branch
92	- [d:r:i] `translate`
93	  - carry a contract across runtime or host-shape differences
94	- [d:r:i] `observe`
95	  - disclose posture, divergence, or current carry state without forcing write-side action
96	- [d:r:i] `adapt`
97	  - change the harness or host behavior in response to stronger evidence
98	- [d:r:i] `sediment`
99	  - stabilize a result into doctrine, carrier, or governance form
100	- [d:r:i] `deploy`
101	  - make the modifier/install path travel into real host contexts
102	
103	## Interpretation Rules
104	
105	- [d:r:i] Do not use `uplift` as a singular umbrella when the target or mode matters materially.
106	- [d:r:i] If a slice changes how the modifier governs host planning artifacts, that is usually:
107	  - harness-contract uplift
108	  - by neutralization or externalization
109	  - in service of host-artifact uplift
110	- [d:r:i] If a slice changes how the improvement program handles horizons, open questions, overlap, or later revision, that is harness-agential and/or harness-operational uplift, not host-artifact uplift.
111	- [d:r:i] If a slice changes deployability, compatibility, or later standalone travel, that belongs to distribution/deployability uplift even when it reuses host-artifact evidence.
112

Date: 2026-04-22
Status: active doctrine note

# Harness Uplift Semantics And Target-Mode Split

## Role

- [d:r:i] This note fixes a recurring semantic blur around the word `uplift`.
- [d:r:i] Its job is to distinguish what is being uplifted, in what sense, and by what mode, so later extraction, deployability, host-artifact, and harness-agential work do not get misread as one flattened family.

## Why This Note Exists

- [d:r:i] The workspace currently contains three overlapping projects:
  - the `prix-guesser` host product
  - the repo-local harness-modifier development program
  - the later standalone/distributable harness-modifier project
- [d:r:i] When those are not kept distinct, host-product horizon carriers can be over-read as harness-program horizon carriers, and host-artifact uplift can be misread as harness-agential improvement.

## Uplift Targets

### 1. Harness-Contract Uplift

- [d:r:i] The target is the harness as a contract-bearing system:
  - workflows
  - skills
  - registries
  - helper boundaries
  - installer/materialization logic
  - propagation routes
  - review routes
  - extraction seams

### 2. Host-Artifact Uplift

- [d:r:i] The target is the host repo's existing operational corpus:
  - `.planning/STATE.md`
  - `.planning/phases/*`
  - uplift memory
  - runtime directories
  - seed corpora
  - migration packets
- [d:r:i] This is the family that keeps a host repo runnable or more readable under the modified harness.

### 3. Harness-Agential Uplift

- [d:r:i] The target is the harness as a software-development / project / planning machine.
- [d:r:i] This includes:
  - handling multiple horizons without blur
  - adapting to new evidence without drift
  - preserving promising futures without premature closure
  - routing deferred/open findings more cleanly
  - carrying long-horizon orientation while remaining revisable

### 4. Harness-Operational Uplift

- [d:r:i] The target is the improvement program's own execution posture:
  - launch truth
  - inheritance/disposition
  - timing calibration
  - overlap discipline
  - sub-agent onboarding and continuity
  - governance/admin carry while lanes run

### 5. Harness-Adaptive Uplift

- [d:r:i] The target is post-deploy learning and correction:
  - discrepancy capture
  - semantic signal capture
  - expectation-versus-observation comparison
  - doctrine sedimentation
  - adaptive correction loops

### 6. Distribution / Deployability Uplift

- [d:r:i] The target is travel across host repos and runtimes:
  - extraction into its own repo
  - installability
  - compatibility declaration
  - host-context testing breadth
  - deployment and upgrade surfaces

## Uplift Modes

- [d:r:i] `neutralize`
  - remove host-local or helper-local literals so a cleaner carrier can own them
- [d:r:i] `externalize`
  - move a contract, policy, or grammar into a named carrier
- [d:r:i] `propagate`
  - carry a changed contract through its neighboring producer / consumer / registry / governance surfaces
- [d:r:i] `classify`
  - distinguish cases that should not yet be collapsed into one branch
- [d:r:i] `translate`
  - carry a contract across runtime or host-shape differences
- [d:r:i] `observe`
  - disclose posture, divergence, or current carry state without forcing write-side action
- [d:r:i] `adapt`
  - change the harness or host behavior in response to stronger evidence
- [d:r:i] `sediment`
  - stabilize a result into doctrine, carrier, or governance form
- [d:r:i] `deploy`
  - make the modifier/install path travel into real host contexts

## Interpretation Rules

- [d:r:i] Do not use `uplift` as a singular umbrella when the target or mode matters materially.
- [d:r:i] If a slice changes how the modifier governs host planning artifacts, that is usually:
  - harness-contract uplift
  - by neutralization or externalization
  - in service of host-artifact uplift
- [d:r:i] If a slice changes how the improvement program handles horizons, open questions, overlap, or later revision, that is harness-agential and/or harness-operational uplift, not host-artifact uplift.
- [d:r:i] If a slice changes deployability, compatibility, or later standalone travel, that belongs to distribution/deployability uplift even when it reuses host-artifact evidence.

## Current Concrete Example

- [d:r:i] [../../../../harness_modifier/uplift/state_section.json](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/uplift/state_section.json) and [../../../../harness_modifier/uplift/phase_layout.json](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/uplift/phase_layout.json) are not primarily host-product horizon doctrine.
- [d:r:i] They are modifier-owned carriers created during harness development.
- [d:r:i] Their target is deployed host-artifact uplift:
  - how the modifier reads and writes host planning artifacts
  - not how `prix-guesser` chooses its own long-horizon product direction

## Anti-Misread Rules

- [d:r:i] Host-product planning docs are not the default horizon carriers for the harness-improvement program.
- [d:r:i] A development-time extraction of a deployed contract is not category confusion by itself; it becomes confusing only when the target/mode split is left unnamed.
- [d:r:i] Later extraction into its own repo is partly a packaging move and partly a semantic-sovereignty move.

## Immediate Consequence

- [d:r:i] Use this note when reading or writing later extraction, deployability, responsible-closure, and host-uplift proposals.
- [d:r:i] If a later note says `uplift` without the target or mode being inferable from context, sharpen it rather than letting the ambiguity ride.

4	# Harness Parallelization Opportunity Map
5	
6	## Role
7	
8	- [d:r:i] This note maps two different parallelization fields that should not be collapsed:
9	  - parallelization inside the modified harness in action
10	  - parallelization inside harness-modifier development and uplift work

14	
15	- [d:r:i] Time pressure is real.
16	- [d:r:i] The answer is not sloppy acceleration.
17	- [d:r:i] The answer is better-designed overlap, better task partitioning, and clearer rules about what can travel in parallel without degrading software quality, continuity, or judgment.
18	- [d:r:i] This note is not a completed diagnosis of vanilla GSD or of the modified harness.
19	- [d:r:i] It is a framing map plus a prompt for a stronger field-mapping pass.
20	
21	## Existing Baselines
22	
23	### Domain Split
24	
25	- [d:r:i] `Harness in action`
26	  - means the modified harness as it operates on real project work:
27	    - discuss
28	    - research
29	    - plan
30	    - execute
31	    - verify
32	    - lateral supporting workflows
33	- [d:r:i] `Harness-improvement program`
34	  - means the work of developing, auditing, extracting, propagating, and governing the harness modifier itself
35	- [d:r:i] These two domains can inform each other, but they are not the same parallelization question and should not be routed through one flattened judgment.
36	- [d:r:i] The examples below are provisional current references, not exhaustive or sovereign claims about the total parallelization posture of vanilla GSD or the modified harness.
37	
38	### Harness In Action
39	
40	- [d:r:i] One visible current example is execution-wave splitting inside phase execution.
41	- [d:r:i] There may be other real or latent parallelization carriers in vanilla GSD and in the modified harness, but this note does not yet claim to have mapped them fully.
42	
43	### Harness-Improvement Program
44	
45	- [d:r:i] This workspace already carries one explicit overlap doctrine:
46	  - [../AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md](../AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md) `Bounded Parallelization And Overlap`
47	- [d:r:i] That doctrine currently governs:
48	  - what can happen while external lanes run
49	  - what must wait for inheritance
50	  - what admin/governance work can safely travel alongside long-running reviews
51	
52	## Opportunity Classes
53	
54	### 1. Phase-Internal Execution Parallelization
55	
56	- [d:r:i] Current baseline:
57	  - wave-based execution after planning has already assigned disjoint work
58	- [d:r:i] This remains the cleanest existing parallelization form because the plan itself encodes the partition.
59	
60	### 2. Pre-Execution Research / Mapping Parallelization
61	
62	- [d:r:i] Opportunity:
63	  - split bounded terrain questions
64	  - split codebase mapping across disjoint subsystems
65	  - split comparative research questions
66	- [d:r:i] Earned when:
67	  - the top-level framing is already coherent
68	  - the sub-questions are genuinely separable
69	  - the parent thread retains synthesis ownership
70	
71	### 3. Verification-Family Parallelization
72	
73	- [d:r:i] Opportunity:
74	  - code review
75	  - security review
76	  - validation gap checks
77	  - propagation review
78	  - docs verification
79	- [d:r:i] Earned when:
80	  - implementation is frozen enough for bounded review
81	  - each review has a clear subject and output carrier
82	
83	### 4. Cross-Phase Parallelization
84	
85	- [d:r:i] Opportunity exists, but only in a narrower form than `execute multiple phases at once`.
86	- [d:r:i] Responsible forms include:
87	  - preparatory research for a later phase on a frozen upstream basis
88	  - bounded spec or mapping work for a later phase when dependencies are already explicit
89	  - adjacent documentation / verification / telemetry work for an earlier completed phase while a new phase is in planning
90	- [d:r:i] Unsafe forms include:
91	  - executing a later phase whose requirements depend on an unsettled earlier phase
92	  - letting later-phase exploratory work harden into canon before the earlier phase settles the boundary
93	
94	### 5. Lateral Workflow Parallelization
95	
96	- [d:r:i] Opportunity:
97	  - lifecycle / propagation refresh work
98	  - review-route work
99	  - deployability preparation
100	  - telemetry / discrepancy carrier work
101	  - governance/admin updates
102	- [d:r:i] This matters because the harness is not only `discuss -> research -> plan -> execute -> verify`.
103	- [d:r:i] It also contains lateral workflows whose work can sometimes travel in parallel with the main line if their basis is frozen and their outputs stay bounded.
104	
105	### 6. Harness-Improvement Program Overlap
106	
107	- [d:r:i] Opportunity:
108	  - while an Opus lane reads a frozen basis, do unrelated governance carry, propagation refreshes, or bounded implementation on another already-settled family
109	  - use bounded sub-agents for classification, packet assembly, or narrower gap-identification while the parent thread retains composition ownership
110	- [d:r:i] This is already partly governed, but not yet mapped as one broader opportunity field.
111	
112	## Domain Rule
113	
114	- [d:r:i] If the question is `can the harness itself do more work in parallel when operating on a host project?`, route it through the `Harness In Action` classes above.
115	- [d:r:i] If the question is `can the harness-improvement program move faster or more cleanly by overlapping audits, implementation, governance carry, or delegated sub-work?`, route it through `Harness-Improvement Program Overlap`.
116	- [d:r:i] If a later note says only `parallelization` without naming which domain it means, sharpen the domain explicitly before using the note to justify design changes.
117	
118	## Representation Rule
119	
120	- [d:r:i] A parallelization map is more useful here than one scalar `parallelize more` doctrine.
121	- [d:r:i] The useful representation is:
122	  - opportunity class
123	  - prerequisite stability
124	  - ownership boundary
125	  - expected gains
126	  - likely risks
127	  - what carrier should preserve the result
128	
129	## Anti-Patterns
130	
131	- [d:r:i] launching parallel work before the governing boundary is coherent
132	- [d:r:i] treating `it could run in parallel` as if it should
133	- [d:r:i] letting delegated work collapse back into the parent thread without explicit disposition
134	- [d:r:i] using parallelization to hide admin/governance debt rather than carrying it
135	- [d:r:i] letting later-phase work become de facto canon before earlier-phase decisions settle
136	
137	## Near Consequence
138	
139	- [d:r:i] The next stronger move is not yet to rewrite multiple live workflows for parallelization.
140	- [d:r:i] The next stronger move is to run a proper field-mapping / diagnosis pass rather than treating the examples here as if they were already a full posture map.
141	- [d:r:i] That diagnosis should ask separately:
142	  - inside vanilla GSD, where parallelization is already explicit, implicit, absent, or artificially constrained
143	  - inside the modified harness, where new parallelization opportunities, frictions, or regressions have been introduced
144	  - inside the harness-improvement program, which overlap/delegation forms are already governed and which still rely too heavily on operator memory
145	- [d:r:i] Only after that diagnosis should later workflow rewrites, agent/protocol changes, or stronger operator-surface changes be judged.

- [d:r:i] This is already partly governed, but not yet mapped as one broader opportunity field.

## Domain Rule

- [d:r:i] If the question is `can the harness itself do more work in parallel when operating on a host project?`, route it through the `Harness In Action` classes above.
- [d:r:i] If the question is `can the harness-improvement program move faster or more cleanly by overlapping audits, implementation, governance carry, or delegated sub-work?`, route it through `Harness-Improvement Program Overlap`.
- [d:r:i] If a later note says only `parallelization` without naming which domain it means, sharpen the domain explicitly before using the note to justify design changes.

## Representation Rule

- [d:r:i] A parallelization map is more useful here than one scalar `parallelize more` doctrine.
- [d:r:i] The useful representation is:
  - opportunity class
  - prerequisite stability
  - ownership boundary
  - expected gains
  - likely risks
  - what carrier should preserve the result

## Anti-Patterns

- [d:r:i] launching parallel work before the governing boundary is coherent
- [d:r:i] treating `it could run in parallel` as if it should
- [d:r:i] letting delegated work collapse back into the parent thread without explicit disposition
- [d:r:i] using parallelization to hide admin/governance debt rather than carrying it
- [d:r:i] letting later-phase work become de facto canon before earlier-phase decisions settle

## Near Consequence

- [d:r:i] The next stronger move is not yet to rewrite multiple live workflows for parallelization.
- [d:r:i] The next stronger move is to run a proper field-mapping / diagnosis pass rather than treating the examples here as if they were already a full posture map.
- [d:r:i] That diagnosis should ask separately:
  - inside vanilla GSD, where parallelization is already explicit, implicit, absent, or artificially constrained
  - inside the modified harness, where new parallelization opportunities, frictions, or regressions have been introduced
  - inside the harness-improvement program, which overlap/delegation forms are already governed and which still rely too heavily on operator memory
- [d:r:i] Only after that diagnosis should later workflow rewrites, agent/protocol changes, or stronger operator-surface changes be judged.

5	
6	## Domain Split
7	
8	- [g:r:i] Responsible closure is a layered field, not one scalar. The strongest representation preserves six uplift targets rather than collapsing them under one "ship-readiness" heading. Borrowed from [intervention-proposals/162](../../intervention-proposals/162-harness-uplift-semantics-and-target-mode-split.md):
9	  - [d:r:i] `harness-contract` — the workflow / skill / registry / overlay / installer contract surface. Already moving under [141](../../intervention-proposals/141-harness-modifier-compatibility-declaration-carrier-implementation.md), [148](../../intervention-proposals/148-harness-modifier-first-overlay-filesystem-rehome-implementation.md), and [159](../../intervention-proposals/159-harness-modifier-project-uplift-host-planning-shape-neutralization-implementation.md).
10	  - [d:r:i] `host-artifact` — how the modifier reads/writes a host's operational corpus (`.planning/STATE.md`, `.planning/phases/*`, seed corpora, uplift memory). Distinct from host-product horizon work.
11	  - [d:r:i] `harness-agential` — the program-as-software-development-machine surface: horizon routing, deferred-finding governance, future-preservation under revision. Carriers at [163](../../intervention-proposals/163-harness-program-horizons-and-future-carry-doctrine.md) and the harness register.
12	  - [d:r:i] `harness-operational` — launch-truth, inheritance/disposition, timing calibration, overlap discipline, lane-packet scaffolding, sub-agent continuity.
13	  - [d:r:i] `harness-adaptive` — post-deploy learning: discrepancy capture, expected-vs-observed comparison, positive-gain signal capture, doctrine sedimentation.
14	  - [d:r:i] `distribution/deployability` — extraction cleanliness, installability, compatibility declaration, host-context testing breadth, update/upgrade surfaces, second-host exercise.
15	- [g:r:i] The uplift-mode vocabulary from `162` should also travel: neutralization, externalization, and propagation have been the recent dominant modes; `deploy`, `adapt`, and `sediment` become live once the payload-home boundary ([160](../../intervention-proposals/160-harness-modifier-project-uplift-post-host-planning-shape-payload-home-judgment-proposal.md)) settles.
16	- [g:r:i] Responsible closure is not the intersection of these surfaces becoming "complete." It is the program carrying all six explicitly so later reviews can re-shape any one surface without dissolving the others. A gain in one surface should not be allowed to silently finish the field.
17	- [d:r:i] Anti-misread fence: closure here is a layered carry, not a finish line. The anti-threshold posture from [AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/AGENTS.md) and [CLAUDE.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/CLAUDE.md) applies directly — do not let `ready to deploy`, `deployable enough`, or `passes host-context tests` become the master frame.
18	
19	## Deployability And Host-Context Testing
20	
21	- [e:c+r:i] The deployability bundle already has three travel-ready artifacts produced by prior slices. Later deployment pressure should inherit these rather than reopen them:
22	  - [e:c:i] typed compatibility carrier at [harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.json](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.json) with posture / runtime_basis / held_annotations / overlay_schema_version / uplift_manifest_schema_version / upstream_compatibility_window / parity_scan_baseline / check_protocol / held_later, and loader at [harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.py) ([141](../../intervention-proposals/141-harness-modifier-compatibility-declaration-carrier-implementation.md)).
23	  - [e:c:i] authoritative source-home split for the first specialist overlay tranche at `harness_modifier/overlay/get-shit-done/workflows/*` and `harness_modifier/overlay/skills/*/SKILL.md` with contract authority at [harness_modifier/contract/portable_gsd_contract.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/contract/portable_gsd_contract.py) ([148](../../intervention-proposals/148-harness-modifier-first-overlay-filesystem-rehome-implementation.md)).
24	  - [e:c:i] typed host-planning-shape externalization under `harness_modifier/uplift/state_section.{json,py}`, `phase_layout.{json,py}`, `state_writer.py`, `output_policy.json` ([159](../../intervention-proposals/159-harness-modifier-project-uplift-host-planning-shape-neutralization-implementation.md)).
25	- [d:r:i] The target host field is `{.codex, .claude, mixed .codex+.claude, host carrying regular GSD, host carrying pre-existing GSD Reflect artifacts that need translation/coexistence}`. Widening into `--gemini` / `--opencode` / generic multi-provider is out of bounds — [GSD Reflect 1.19.8](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/CHANGELOG.md) deprecated those install paths for good reasons, and the modifier should not re-import that complexity.
26	- [d:r:i] The stronger minimum deployability bundle before broader deployment or extraction pressure is earned is a layered set, not one artifact:
27	  - closed payload-home judgment per [160](../../intervention-proposals/160-harness-modifier-project-uplift-post-host-planning-shape-payload-home-judgment-proposal.md) — what materially still binds the helper to the host vs what is portable modifier payload
28	  - at least one observe-only second-host dry-run against a disjoint `.codex`-only host, capturing what the declaration's `check_protocol` refuses / warns / shifts-mode on
29	  - at least one observe-only dry-run against a mixed `.codex` + held-annotation `.claude` host, so the held-annotation posture from [141](../../intervention-proposals/141-harness-modifier-compatibility-declaration-carrier-implementation.md) is exercised, not left as prose
30	  - a single-writer governance-surface enumeration inherited from the parallelization field map, extended to cover the surfaces closure and deployment lanes will concurrently touch (`CURRENT-STATE.md`, `STATUS.md`, `INDEX.md`, `AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md`, `HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md`, `.planning/STATE.md`, `.planning/UPLIFT-REPORT.md`, `.planning/UPLIFT-MANIFEST.json`)
31	  - an explicit deferred-carry slot for the cross-vendor responsible-closure audit ([161 commitment #6](../../intervention-proposals/161-harness-modifier-responsible-closure-deployability-and-adaptive-feedback-route.md)) scheduled against the payload-home closure, so it is held rather than wished.
32	- [d:r:i] Host-context testing breadth should not collapse into "the installer ran green." It should record what the declaration said, what the host returned, where the `observed_basis_only` compatibility window held, and where held-annotation `.claude` posture produced divergence.
33	- [d:r:i] First deployment exercise should explicitly stay observe-only. `verify-materialized --strict` and the runtime-visibility snapshot are the default reads; no write-side installer claim against a non-prix-guesser host yet.
34	
35	## Adaptive Feedback, Measurement, And Telemetry
36	
37	- [g:r:i] The measurement layer should keep signal classes separated rather than collapse into one scalar success metric, pass/fail tally, or positive/negative tally. Named families for the first responsible-closure slice:
38	  - [d:r:i] `deployment-context` — runtime basis, installed harness version, `manifest_schema_version`, parity-scan baseline, declaration posture at the moment of install
39	  - [d:r:i] `expectation-vs-observation` — what the `check_protocol` was asked to do and what actually returned (refuse / warn / shift-mode / accept)
40	  - [d:r:i] `semantic-deviation` — overlay carrier travelled but consumer diverged, or contract-mismatch vectors like refmap drift, parity-classifier disagreement, or overlay-vs-install-target divergence
41	  - [d:r:i] `positive-gain` — uplift that increased carry at a seam (externalization closed a host-shape literal, propagation updated N neighbor surfaces coherently, neutralization removed a helper-local literal). Recorded as its own class so later telemetry does not degrade into breakage tallies.
42	  - [d:r:i] `measurement-provenance` — who/what wrote the observation, from what session / model / runtime / harness, so the observation itself carries enough context to be re-audited.
43	- [e:c+r:i] GSD Reflect is a reference field here, not the ceiling. Absorb these shapes:
44	  - [e:c:i] split-provenance v2 (`detected_by` vs `written_by` as separate signature objects, with `not_available` discipline for missing facts) per [commands/gsd/signal.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/commands/gsd/signal.md) and [CHANGELOG 1.19.6](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/CHANGELOG.md)
45	  - [e:c:i] signal-type taxonomy (`deviation` / `struggle` / `config-mismatch` / `capability-gap` / `custom`) and durability ladder (`workaround` / `convention` / `principle`)
46	  - [e:c:i] canonical `automation_skip_reasons` vocabulary from [feature-manifest.json](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/get-shit-done/feature-manifest.json) as a shape for enumerating install-path skip/refuse reasons
47	  - [e:c:i] automation-level stack (0=manual, 1=nudge, 2=prompt, 3=auto) as a way to declare which telemetry carriers run on operator command and which could later auto-run
48	  - [e:c:i] soft-target / rigor-gate stance on volume (no hard cap, quality enforced by rigor rather than quantity) as a posture for responsible closure's own observation log
49	- [d:r:i] Do not import wholesale: `gsd-tools telemetry` subcommand module, the sensor → synthesizer → reflector pipeline, per-phase signal caps, auto-collection / reentrancy locks, cross-project KB aggregation, lifecycle state machines, or the `session_meta_postlude` hook install wiring. Those are protected futures, not pending work.
50	- [d:r:i] Measurement side-effects that should be governed rather than left as ambient runtime traces:
51	  - session/runtime signature attached to every observation (what wrote it, from what basis)
52	  - disposition verb per return (`accept` / `revise` / `park` / `reject`) so observations are not silently inherited
53	  - launch-truth capture for doctrine-sensitive observations per [AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/AGENTS.md) `Delegation And Orchestration`
54	- [d:r:i] First telemetry slice should be narrower than the full field: one durable carrier scoped to `deployment-context` + `expectation-vs-observation` + `semantic-deviation` + `positive-gain` + `measurement-provenance` families, observe-only, operator-triggered, single-writer, keyed to one host exercise. What it intentionally does not yet carry: auto-collection hooks, reentrancy-locked sensor daemons, reflector/synthesizer agents, per-phase cap enforcement, cross-project aggregation, lifecycle state transitions, automation-level 3 escalation.
55	
56	## Discrepancy, Positive Gain, And Semantic Signal Capture
57	
58	- [d:r:i] Discrepancy carriers should distinguish at least four vectors so later review does not collapse them into one "broken" bucket:
59	  - `contract-mismatch` — declaration asserted X, host observed Y (compatibility-window violation, schema-version mismatch, basis outside declared support)
60	  - `overlay-authority-drift` — modifier-owned source ships one shape, install-target mirror diverges (catches manifest/source desync the authority split from [148](../../intervention-proposals/148-harness-modifier-first-overlay-filesystem-rehome-implementation.md) is specifically designed to surface)
61	  - `refmap/topology drift` — `audit_refmap.py verify` fails after a concurrent lane wrote paths the frozen basis assumed
62	  - `parity-classifier drift` — `.codex` vs held-annotation `.claude` observed posture diverges against the parity_scan_baseline
63	- [d:r:i] Positive-gain carriers should be a first-class class, not a residual of "no discrepancy detected." Concrete examples:
64	  - an `externalize` tranche closed a helper-local literal and now the declaration carries it (evidence: the literal count at `tooling/codex/project_uplift.py` thinned from N to 0 across `154` / `157` / `159`)
65	  - a `propagate` pass updated producer / consumer / registry / governance surfaces coherently (evidence: the propagation registry v2 rows stayed in sync after the slice)
66	  - a `neutralize` tranche removed a host-local embed (evidence: the `.planning/STATE.md` slot shape is now read through a typed carrier rather than a helper constant)
67	- [d:r:i] Semantic signal capture should record what shape the observation broadened, sharpened, intensified, or made more durable — not whether it passed a threshold. This is the anti-threshold posture in telemetry form, and it is the axis GSD Reflect's severity / polarity fields do not directly carry.
68	- [d:r:i] Measurement-provenance carriers should govern the observation itself:
69	  - attach `detected_by` and `written_by` signature objects per [commands/gsd/signal.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/commands/gsd/signal.md) — even when they resolve to the same runtime facts — so manual vs lane-driven origins stay distinguishable later
70	  - record `about_work` (artifact/work under judgment) rather than leaving it as `[]` when the conversation identifies it, so discrepancy and positive-gain observations have explicit subjects
71	  - fall back to `not_available` rather than invention when runtime, model, session, or version are unknown
72	
73	## Harness-Agential Closure Quality
74	
75	- [g:r:i] The horizon stack from [163](../../intervention-proposals/163-harness-program-horizons-and-future-carry-doctrine.md) is load-bearing for responsible closure. Harness-program horizons are separate from host-product horizons; `.planning/LONG-ARC.md` and `.planning/ROADMAP.md` are contextual inputs, not the default sovereign future surface for the harness-improvement program.
76	- [d:r:i] Responsible closure should strengthen five agential surfaces rather than treat them as side-effects of shipping:
77	  - `horizon-routing clarity` — near/medium/far carriers named explicitly per slice so horizon borrowing from host-product docs is caught and corrected
78	  - `deferred/open-finding governance` — findings route into named carriers ([HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md) `Horizon Routing`: active bounded slice / held later / seed / deferred / doctrine / audit-family memory) rather than ambient chat memory
79	  - `future-preservation doctrine` — the protected-futures list from [163](../../intervention-proposals/163-harness-program-horizons-and-future-carry-doctrine.md) stays explicitly open: standalone repo, installer/distribution travel, richer adaptive telemetry, stronger parallelization frameworks, broader host-context deployability. Local convenience in the current slice should not quietly foreclose them.
80	  - `post-review revision grammar` — later audit findings should re-shape the program through near → medium → far revision, not a silent reset of far-horizon ambition or a forced immediate implementation of far-horizon desire
81	  - `operational uplift` — launch-truth capture, disposition verbs, timing-estimate ledgers, lane-packet / spec / prompt / output / inheritance scaffolding per [AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md](../../AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md). Harness-operational quality is not incidental to closure; it is what lets N concurrent external reviewer lanes be individually auditable rather than collapse into folklore.
82	- [d:r:i] Anti-misread fence: agential uplift is not a soft/aesthetic surface next to "real" contract or deployment work. A harness that deploys cleanly but handles revision poorly has not closed responsibly; neither has one that handles revision well but cannot travel.
83	
84	## Parallelization As A Closure Multiplier
85	
86	- [g:r:i] Inherit the three-class taxonomy from [parallelization-audit/outputs/01](../../parallelization-audit/outputs/01-harness-parallelization-field-map-and-diagnosis-audit-opus47-max-r1.md) rather than re-diagnosing from scratch per the packet and the accepted [parallelization-audit/dispositions/01](../../parallelization-audit/dispositions/01-harness-parallelization-field-map-and-diagnosis-audit-inheritance.md):
87	  - `safe earned` — fan-out on a frozen basis with disjoint outputs, companion-carry on unrelated governance surfaces, detect-only specialist lanes
88	  - `promising but not-yet-governed` — review-family wave, pre-execution research split, cross-vendor parity lane, async-parallel cross-AI review
89	  - `likely coherence/quality risk` — parallel writes to single-writer governance surfaces, refmap/topology rewrites during a live lane, installer runs during a live lane, consensus-flattening reviewer fan-out, Phase 01 rerun boundary crossed during a returning lane
90	- [d:r:i] Responsible closure can earn parallelization as a multiplier in three concrete places without reopening workflow rewrites:
91	  - host-context testing breadth — run the `.codex`-only and mixed `.codex+.claude` dry-run lanes concurrently on the same frozen declaration baseline. This is `safe earned`: disjoint hosts, frozen source, observe-only, per-lane output carriers.
92	  - telemetry signal classification — multiple concurrent readers over a frozen install-exercise artifact corpus, each writing to its own signal-class carrier (deployment-context / expectation-vs-observation / semantic-deviation / positive-gain / measurement-provenance). This is `promising but not-yet-governed`: needs a compact fan-out packet shape per the parallelization-audit held-later carry, but the inputs are already partitionable.
93	  - adversarial review on responsible-closure itself — two or more external reviewer lanes on a frozen closure-field-map basis, without consensus-flattening, producing per-lane outputs that route through separate dispositions rather than one consensus synthesis. This is `safe earned` and is exactly the pattern this current audit lane is exercising.
94	- [d:r:i] Parallelization is not a standalone goal here; it is what lets responsible closure widen host-context testing, signal-class capture, and adversarial review without degrading the harness-agential surface. The cross-vendor UI asymmetry (Codex `request_user_input` vs Claude `AskUserQuestion` vs Copilot `vscode_askquestions`) remains a held-later concern for interactive lanes and should not block observe-only dry-runs.
95	- [d:r:i] Do not expand into workflow-level rewrites from this lane. `execute-phase.md`, `review.md`, `map-codebase.md`, `ingest-docs.md`, `diagnose-issues.md`, `manager.md`, and `config.json.parallelization` stay out of scope. The single-writer surface enumeration, the fan-out packet template, and the `Parallelization Impact` extension to `propagation-review.md` remain held-later carries per the parallelization-audit disposition.
96	
97	## What Must Land Before Broader Deployment Pressure
98	
99	- [d:r:i] `160` payload-home judgment closed with an explicit classification of: portable modifier payload / stable compatibility-shim boundary / still-shared install/materialization boundary. Without this, "broader deployment" silently inherits blurred scope.
100	- [d:r:i] Second overlay tranche classification (the overwrite-family source-split decision that [148](../../intervention-proposals/148-harness-modifier-first-overlay-filesystem-rehome-implementation.md) explicitly held later), at least as an opening note — not as implementation.
101	- [d:r:i] One durable bounded observation carrier for the five signal families above. v2_split-style provenance, observe-only, operator-triggered, single-writer. Keyed to one host exercise. No auto-collection, no sensor daemon, no reflector.
102	- [d:r:i] One recorded observe-only dry-run against a disjoint host.
