# Harness Modifier Responsible Closure Field Map

## Domain Split

- [g:r:i] Responsible closure is a layered field, not one scalar. The strongest representation preserves six uplift targets rather than collapsing them under one "ship-readiness" heading. Borrowed from [intervention-proposals/162](../../intervention-proposals/162-harness-uplift-semantics-and-target-mode-split.md):
  - [d:r:i] `harness-contract` — the workflow / skill / registry / overlay / installer contract surface. Already moving under [141](../../intervention-proposals/141-harness-modifier-compatibility-declaration-carrier-implementation.md), [148](../../intervention-proposals/148-harness-modifier-first-overlay-filesystem-rehome-implementation.md), and [159](../../intervention-proposals/159-harness-modifier-project-uplift-host-planning-shape-neutralization-implementation.md).
  - [d:r:i] `host-artifact` — how the modifier reads/writes a host's operational corpus (`.planning/STATE.md`, `.planning/phases/*`, seed corpora, uplift memory). Distinct from host-product horizon work.
  - [d:r:i] `harness-agential` — the program-as-software-development-machine surface: horizon routing, deferred-finding governance, future-preservation under revision. Carriers at [163](../../intervention-proposals/163-harness-program-horizons-and-future-carry-doctrine.md) and the harness register.
  - [d:r:i] `harness-operational` — launch-truth, inheritance/disposition, timing calibration, overlap discipline, lane-packet scaffolding, sub-agent continuity.
  - [d:r:i] `harness-adaptive` — post-deploy learning: discrepancy capture, expected-vs-observed comparison, positive-gain signal capture, doctrine sedimentation.
  - [d:r:i] `distribution/deployability` — extraction cleanliness, installability, compatibility declaration, host-context testing breadth, update/upgrade surfaces, second-host exercise.
- [g:r:i] The uplift-mode vocabulary from `162` should also travel: neutralization, externalization, and propagation have been the recent dominant modes; `deploy`, `adapt`, and `sediment` become live once the payload-home boundary ([160](../../intervention-proposals/160-harness-modifier-project-uplift-post-host-planning-shape-payload-home-judgment-proposal.md)) settles.
- [g:r:i] Responsible closure is not the intersection of these surfaces becoming "complete." It is the program carrying all six explicitly so later reviews can re-shape any one surface without dissolving the others. A gain in one surface should not be allowed to silently finish the field.
- [d:r:i] Anti-misread fence: closure here is a layered carry, not a finish line. The anti-threshold posture from [AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/AGENTS.md) and [CLAUDE.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/CLAUDE.md) applies directly — do not let `ready to deploy`, `deployable enough`, or `passes host-context tests` become the master frame.

## Deployability And Host-Context Testing

- [e:c+r:i] The deployability bundle already has three travel-ready artifacts produced by prior slices. Later deployment pressure should inherit these rather than reopen them:
  - [e:c:i] typed compatibility carrier at [harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.json](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.json) with posture / runtime_basis / held_annotations / overlay_schema_version / uplift_manifest_schema_version / upstream_compatibility_window / parity_scan_baseline / check_protocol / held_later, and loader at [harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.py) ([141](../../intervention-proposals/141-harness-modifier-compatibility-declaration-carrier-implementation.md)).
  - [e:c:i] authoritative source-home split for the first specialist overlay tranche at `harness_modifier/overlay/get-shit-done/workflows/*` and `harness_modifier/overlay/skills/*/SKILL.md` with contract authority at [harness_modifier/contract/portable_gsd_contract.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/contract/portable_gsd_contract.py) ([148](../../intervention-proposals/148-harness-modifier-first-overlay-filesystem-rehome-implementation.md)).
  - [e:c:i] typed host-planning-shape externalization under `harness_modifier/uplift/state_section.{json,py}`, `phase_layout.{json,py}`, `state_writer.py`, `output_policy.json` ([159](../../intervention-proposals/159-harness-modifier-project-uplift-host-planning-shape-neutralization-implementation.md)).
- [d:r:i] The target host field is `{.codex, .claude, mixed .codex+.claude, host carrying regular GSD, host carrying pre-existing GSD Reflect artifacts that need translation/coexistence}`. Widening into `--gemini` / `--opencode` / generic multi-provider is out of bounds — [GSD Reflect 1.19.8](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/CHANGELOG.md) deprecated those install paths for good reasons, and the modifier should not re-import that complexity.
- [d:r:i] The stronger minimum deployability bundle before broader deployment or extraction pressure is earned is a layered set, not one artifact:
  - closed payload-home judgment per [160](../../intervention-proposals/160-harness-modifier-project-uplift-post-host-planning-shape-payload-home-judgment-proposal.md) — what materially still binds the helper to the host vs what is portable modifier payload
  - at least one observe-only second-host dry-run against a disjoint `.codex`-only host, capturing what the declaration's `check_protocol` refuses / warns / shifts-mode on
  - at least one observe-only dry-run against a mixed `.codex` + held-annotation `.claude` host, so the held-annotation posture from [141](../../intervention-proposals/141-harness-modifier-compatibility-declaration-carrier-implementation.md) is exercised, not left as prose
  - a single-writer governance-surface enumeration inherited from the parallelization field map, extended to cover the surfaces closure and deployment lanes will concurrently touch (`CURRENT-STATE.md`, `STATUS.md`, `INDEX.md`, `AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md`, `HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md`, `.planning/STATE.md`, `.planning/UPLIFT-REPORT.md`, `.planning/UPLIFT-MANIFEST.json`)
  - an explicit deferred-carry slot for the cross-vendor responsible-closure audit ([161 commitment #6](../../intervention-proposals/161-harness-modifier-responsible-closure-deployability-and-adaptive-feedback-route.md)) scheduled against the payload-home closure, so it is held rather than wished.
- [d:r:i] Host-context testing breadth should not collapse into "the installer ran green." It should record what the declaration said, what the host returned, where the `observed_basis_only` compatibility window held, and where held-annotation `.claude` posture produced divergence.
- [d:r:i] First deployment exercise should explicitly stay observe-only. `verify-materialized --strict` and the runtime-visibility snapshot are the default reads; no write-side installer claim against a non-prix-guesser host yet.

## Adaptive Feedback, Measurement, And Telemetry

- [g:r:i] The measurement layer should keep signal classes separated rather than collapse into one scalar success metric, pass/fail tally, or positive/negative tally. Named families for the first responsible-closure slice:
  - [d:r:i] `deployment-context` — runtime basis, installed harness version, `manifest_schema_version`, parity-scan baseline, declaration posture at the moment of install
  - [d:r:i] `expectation-vs-observation` — what the `check_protocol` was asked to do and what actually returned (refuse / warn / shift-mode / accept)
  - [d:r:i] `semantic-deviation` — overlay carrier travelled but consumer diverged, or contract-mismatch vectors like refmap drift, parity-classifier disagreement, or overlay-vs-install-target divergence
  - [d:r:i] `positive-gain` — uplift that increased carry at a seam (externalization closed a host-shape literal, propagation updated N neighbor surfaces coherently, neutralization removed a helper-local literal). Recorded as its own class so later telemetry does not degrade into breakage tallies.
  - [d:r:i] `measurement-provenance` — who/what wrote the observation, from what session / model / runtime / harness, so the observation itself carries enough context to be re-audited.
- [e:c+r:i] GSD Reflect is a reference field here, not the ceiling. Absorb these shapes:
  - [e:c:i] split-provenance v2 (`detected_by` vs `written_by` as separate signature objects, with `not_available` discipline for missing facts) per [commands/gsd/signal.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/commands/gsd/signal.md) and [CHANGELOG 1.19.6](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/CHANGELOG.md)
  - [e:c:i] signal-type taxonomy (`deviation` / `struggle` / `config-mismatch` / `capability-gap` / `custom`) and durability ladder (`workaround` / `convention` / `principle`)
  - [e:c:i] canonical `automation_skip_reasons` vocabulary from [feature-manifest.json](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/get-shit-done/feature-manifest.json) as a shape for enumerating install-path skip/refuse reasons
  - [e:c:i] automation-level stack (0=manual, 1=nudge, 2=prompt, 3=auto) as a way to declare which telemetry carriers run on operator command and which could later auto-run
  - [e:c:i] soft-target / rigor-gate stance on volume (no hard cap, quality enforced by rigor rather than quantity) as a posture for responsible closure's own observation log
- [d:r:i] Do not import wholesale: `gsd-tools telemetry` subcommand module, the sensor → synthesizer → reflector pipeline, per-phase signal caps, auto-collection / reentrancy locks, cross-project KB aggregation, lifecycle state machines, or the `session_meta_postlude` hook install wiring. Those are protected futures, not pending work.
- [d:r:i] Measurement side-effects that should be governed rather than left as ambient runtime traces:
  - session/runtime signature attached to every observation (what wrote it, from what basis)
  - disposition verb per return (`accept` / `revise` / `park` / `reject`) so observations are not silently inherited
  - launch-truth capture for doctrine-sensitive observations per [AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/AGENTS.md) `Delegation And Orchestration`
- [d:r:i] First telemetry slice should be narrower than the full field: one durable carrier scoped to `deployment-context` + `expectation-vs-observation` + `semantic-deviation` + `positive-gain` + `measurement-provenance` families, observe-only, operator-triggered, single-writer, keyed to one host exercise. What it intentionally does not yet carry: auto-collection hooks, reentrancy-locked sensor daemons, reflector/synthesizer agents, per-phase cap enforcement, cross-project aggregation, lifecycle state transitions, automation-level 3 escalation.

## Discrepancy, Positive Gain, And Semantic Signal Capture

- [d:r:i] Discrepancy carriers should distinguish at least four vectors so later review does not collapse them into one "broken" bucket:
  - `contract-mismatch` — declaration asserted X, host observed Y (compatibility-window violation, schema-version mismatch, basis outside declared support)
  - `overlay-authority-drift` — modifier-owned source ships one shape, install-target mirror diverges (catches manifest/source desync the authority split from [148](../../intervention-proposals/148-harness-modifier-first-overlay-filesystem-rehome-implementation.md) is specifically designed to surface)
  - `refmap/topology drift` — `audit_refmap.py verify` fails after a concurrent lane wrote paths the frozen basis assumed
  - `parity-classifier drift` — `.codex` vs held-annotation `.claude` observed posture diverges against the parity_scan_baseline
- [d:r:i] Positive-gain carriers should be a first-class class, not a residual of "no discrepancy detected." Concrete examples:
  - an `externalize` tranche closed a helper-local literal and now the declaration carries it (evidence: the literal count at `tooling/codex/project_uplift.py` thinned from N to 0 across `154` / `157` / `159`)
  - a `propagate` pass updated producer / consumer / registry / governance surfaces coherently (evidence: the propagation registry v2 rows stayed in sync after the slice)
  - a `neutralize` tranche removed a host-local embed (evidence: the `.planning/STATE.md` slot shape is now read through a typed carrier rather than a helper constant)
- [d:r:i] Semantic signal capture should record what shape the observation broadened, sharpened, intensified, or made more durable — not whether it passed a threshold. This is the anti-threshold posture in telemetry form, and it is the axis GSD Reflect's severity / polarity fields do not directly carry.
- [d:r:i] Measurement-provenance carriers should govern the observation itself:
  - attach `detected_by` and `written_by` signature objects per [commands/gsd/signal.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/get-shit-done-reflect/commands/gsd/signal.md) — even when they resolve to the same runtime facts — so manual vs lane-driven origins stay distinguishable later
  - record `about_work` (artifact/work under judgment) rather than leaving it as `[]` when the conversation identifies it, so discrepancy and positive-gain observations have explicit subjects
  - fall back to `not_available` rather than invention when runtime, model, session, or version are unknown

## Harness-Agential Closure Quality

- [g:r:i] The horizon stack from [163](../../intervention-proposals/163-harness-program-horizons-and-future-carry-doctrine.md) is load-bearing for responsible closure. Harness-program horizons are separate from host-product horizons; `.planning/LONG-ARC.md` and `.planning/ROADMAP.md` are contextual inputs, not the default sovereign future surface for the harness-improvement program.
- [d:r:i] Responsible closure should strengthen five agential surfaces rather than treat them as side-effects of shipping:
  - `horizon-routing clarity` — near/medium/far carriers named explicitly per slice so horizon borrowing from host-product docs is caught and corrected
  - `deferred/open-finding governance` — findings route into named carriers ([HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md) `Horizon Routing`: active bounded slice / held later / seed / deferred / doctrine / audit-family memory) rather than ambient chat memory
  - `future-preservation doctrine` — the protected-futures list from [163](../../intervention-proposals/163-harness-program-horizons-and-future-carry-doctrine.md) stays explicitly open: standalone repo, installer/distribution travel, richer adaptive telemetry, stronger parallelization frameworks, broader host-context deployability. Local convenience in the current slice should not quietly foreclose them.
  - `post-review revision grammar` — later audit findings should re-shape the program through near → medium → far revision, not a silent reset of far-horizon ambition or a forced immediate implementation of far-horizon desire

# Harness Parallelization Field Map And Diagnosis

## Domain Split

- [g:r:i] Three fields, not one. Keep these separate:
  - [d:r:i] `vanilla GSD in action`
    - parallelization baked into upstream workflow grammar (wave execution, parallel mappers, classifier fan-outs, background Task agents, cross-phase workstreams)
    - governed mainly by `config.json.parallelization`, wave frontmatter, and per-workflow fan-out rules
  - [d:r:i] `modified harness in action`
    - the same vanilla surface as it travels under `.codex/`, overlay skills, harness-modifier carriers, AGENTS/CLAUDE wrappers, and the launch-truth / timing-estimate / propagation-review / runtime-visibility toolkit
    - governed additionally by root [AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/AGENTS.md) `Delegation And Orchestration`, planning-local [.planning/AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/AGENTS.md), and the repo-local contract-propagation doctrine
  - [d:r:i] `harness-improvement program overlap`
    - how the improvement program itself overlaps audit lanes, external reviewer work, sub-agent delegation, change-triggered refreshes, governance-carry tranches, and implementation on frozen adjacent families
    - governed by [AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md](../../AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md) `Bounded Parallelization And Overlap`, [HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md) `Horizon Routing`, and the active `intervention-proposals/162-165` semantic split
- [g:r:i] The three fields share vocabulary but not behavior. A `parallelize more` rule in one degrades another. The governing task is classification, boundary naming, and prerequisite disclosure, not one scalar.
- [d:r:i] The strongest representation here is a map of classes, boundaries, and prerequisites rather than one universal rule. The three fields diverge under pressure and later doctrine should preserve the split.

## Vanilla GSD Posture

- [e:c+r:i] Explicit governed parallelization (plan-side, wave-level):
  - [e:c:i] `execute-phase` wave-based parallel execution with intra-wave `files_modified` overlap detection, post-wave hook validation, post-merge test gate, and worktree isolation (`.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/execute-phase.md:334-785`; SDK `phase-runner.ts:579-720`).
  - [e:c:i] Config-surface parallelization knobs: `parallelization.enabled / plan_level / task_level / skip_checkpoints / max_concurrent_agents / min_plans_for_parallel` (`.codex/get-shit-done/templates/config.json:21-28`).
  - [e:c:i] `USE_WORKTREES=false` fallback forces sequential within the main working tree; submodule repos fall back to sequential automatically (`execute-phase.md:85-94`).
- [e:c+r:i] Explicit governed parallelization (lateral / fan-out agents):
  - [e:c:i] `map-codebase` spawns four `gsd-codebase-mapper` agents in parallel with `run_in_background=true`, using a direct-write-to-disk pattern so the orchestrator only collects line counts (`.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/map-codebase.md:101-219`).
  - [e:c:i] `new-project` runs four parallel researcher sessions (`sdk/src/init-runner.ts:4`, `parallelization: true`).
  - [e:c:i] `ingest-docs` spawns one `gsd-doc-classifier` per discovered doc in a single multi-Task message, with sequential fallback for Copilot (`ingest-docs.md:188-207`).
  - [e:c:i] `verify-work -> diagnose-issues` spawns one `gsd-debugger` per UAT gap in parallel on a frozen symptom set (`.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/diagnose-issues.md:86-118`).
  - [e:c:i] `manager` dispatches plan/execute as background `Task(run_in_background=true)` agents while running discuss inline, with a compound "Continue" option enumerating multiple actions at once (`.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/manager.md:56-282`).
  - [e:c:i] `workstreams` provides explicit cross-phase parallel streams with a session-scoped active pointer (`docs/INVENTORY.md:111`, workstream-flag reference).
- [e:r:i] Implied but undernamed / operator-memory-governed parallelization:
  - [d:r:i] The revision loop inside `plan-phase` (planner → plan-checker → revise → plan-checker, up to 3 iterations) is strictly serial, but plan-checker's verification dimensions have disjoint subjects and are bundled into one agent call rather than split.
  - [d:r:i] The post-implementation review family (`code-review`, `secure-phase`, `validate-phase` / `nyquist-auditor`, `ui-review`, `eval-review`, `audit-uat`, `docs-update` verifier) runs one command at a time; each has its own subject and output carrier, and no wave grouping exists across them.
  - [d:r:i] `ai-integration-phase` runs framework-selector → ai-researcher → domain-researcher → eval-planner strictly sequentially (`commands/gsd/ai-integration-phase.md:16-21`); ai-researcher and domain-researcher have disjoint inputs once the framework is chosen.
  - [d:r:i] `autonomous` drives discuss → plan → execute per phase sequentially across a milestone; no cross-phase overlap even when later-phase preparatory research would be safe on a frozen upstream basis.
- [e:r:i] Principled serial (not accidental):
  - [d:r:i] The discuss → research → plan → execute → verify backbone. Each step consumes the prior step's durable output (`CONTEXT.md`, `RESEARCH.md`, `PLAN.md`, `SUMMARY.md`, `VERIFICATION.md`). The SDK `phase-runner.ts` encodes this as one state machine.
  - [d:r:i] Atomic per-task git commits inside `execute-plan.md`: serial within a plan is a deliberate auditability guarantee, not throughput timidity.
  - [d:r:i] Cross-AI review in `review.md` invokes external CLIs sequentially and flags this explicitly as "avoid rate limits"; principled given per-provider keyed quota plus the synthesis step wanting a stable run-home per reviewer (`review.md:172-297`).
- [d:r:i] Accidental / historically inherited serial:
  - [d:r:i] Single `gsd-phase-researcher` per phase. The researcher output is one `RESEARCH.md`, but research questions often partition (domain, integrations, pitfalls, validation strategy); the split-and-synthesize pattern already used in `new-project` and `map-codebase` is not reused here.
  - [d:r:i] Cross-AI review serialization: rate-limits are a real constraint, but per-CLI run-homes and independent stdin-fed prompts are already in place; the "sequential" framing conflates rate-limit pacing with composition ownership.
  - [d:r:i] `audit-uat` reads each phase's UAT.md to build a prioritized list, but reading is done by one agent rather than fan-out plus parent synthesis.
- [d:r:i] Asymmetry vs the modified harness: vanilla GSD treats parallelization as a config-flag plus wave-grammar problem. Overlap discipline beyond the plan wave is implicit; there is no vanilla doctrine corresponding to `Bounded Parallelization And Overlap`.

## Modified Harness Posture

- [e:c+r:i] New opportunities the modifier has opened:
  - [d:r:i] Baseline/delta propagation pair (`intervention-proposals/95`, `96`) partitions review reads: upstream-pristine baseline in one lane, repo-local delta in another, without racing on the same propagation canon.
  - [d:r:i] Detect-only specialist workflows (`uplift-project`, `seed-migration-inventory`, `propagation-review`) default to read-only inspection (`.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/propagation-review.md:1-141`; `workflows/uplift-project.md`; `workflows/seed-migration-inventory.md`). These are safe to run as companion lanes alongside an active main slice.
  - [d:r:i] Frozen durable artifacts (propagation registry v2 pack at `propagation-audit/artifacts/02-06`, runtime-visibility snapshots, `harness_canary.py` reports, `manifest_install_coherence.py` reports) give concurrent readers a stable object without touching live runtime.
  - [d:r:i] Top-level reasoning uplift (`gpt-5.4` `xhigh` for orchestration) plus the research-methodology tier (Codex 5.4 high gathering → xhigh synthesis) give parallel researcher fan-outs more carry per spawn than vanilla profile assumptions.
  - [d:r:i] Launch-truth capture (`capture_launch_truth.py --since`) plus the audit lane scaffolding (opening note / packet / spec / prompt / launch-truth / output / inheritance / comparative disposition / frozen artifacts in [AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md](../../AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md)) make N concurrent external reviewer lanes individually auditable rather than collapsing into folklore.
  - [d:r:i] Change-triggered refresh cadence (`propagation-audit/17-50`) lets mechanical propagation notes land alongside unrelated lanes instead of waiting for a giant catch-up.
- [e:c+r:i] New frictions the modifier introduces:
  - [d:r:i] Top-level orchestration rule forbids recursive GSD call graphs (`AGENTS.md:148-150`). Some naive parallel fan-outs that require nested workflow spawn paths are now illegal; parent thread has to own composition.
  - [d:r:i] Pre-spawn ceremony per agent call: re-read `AGENTS.md`, classify task class, state `agent -> model -> reasoning` mapping, state bounded duration, verify effective launch settings against `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite`, preserve durable launch-truth for doctrine-sensitive work (`AGENTS.md:156-184`). Fan-outs pay this cost per spawn, which thins the "just launch five classifiers in one message" pattern that vanilla `ingest-docs` assumes.
  - [d:r:i] Review-then-disposition gate before committing delegated output (`AGENTS.md:168-178`). Parallel fan-out and parallel disposition are not equivalent; disposition bottlenecks back into the parent thread.
  - [d:r:i] Checkpoint-commit prerequisite before delegating substantial bounded edits (`AGENTS.md:164-167`). Two lanes that want different baselines cannot overlap on the same worktree.
  - [d:r:i] Cross-vendor wrapper translation: `.codex` vs `.claude` ask-question/spawn-agent grammar differs (Claude `Task` + `AskUserQuestion` vs Codex `spawn_agent` + `request_user_input` vs Copilot `vscode_askquestions`; see overlay skill adapters at `harness_modifier/overlay/skills/*/SKILL.md`). An interactive lane that parallels cleanly in Claude Code degrades in Codex.
  - [d:r:i] `.codex/` is the observed basis and `.claude/` is held-annotation (`intervention-proposals/116`, `134`, `135`). Running live parity-driven materialization lanes in parallel across both runtimes is not yet governed.
- [e:c+r:i] New protocol demands:
  - [d:r:i] Launch-truth per doctrine-sensitive spawn, captured to an owning review/disposition carrier before inheriting the return (`AGENTS.md:175-180`; `.planning/AGENTS.md` `Launch-Truth Discipline`).
  - [d:r:i] Timing-estimate ledger per substantial external lane, with post-run calibration note (`AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md` `Timing estimate`).
  - [d:r:i] Explicit disposition verb per return: `accept` / `revise` / `park` / `reject`.
  - [d:r:i] Propagation-review route when a slice crosses producer/consumer families (`.planning/AGENTS.md` `Contract-Propagation Hygiene`; `workflows/propagation-review.md`).
  - [d:r:i] Anti-threshold doctrine: do not let parallel reviewer fan-outs collapse into threshold agreement; keep lone high-signal criticism, merely-adequate areas, and later-audit risks visible even without consensus (`tooling/portable-gsd/overlay/get-shit-done/workflows/review.md:344-375`).
- [e:c+r:i] New risks to continuity and quality:
  - [d:r:i] Single-writer governance surfaces (`CURRENT-STATE.md`, `STATUS.md`, `INDEX.md`, `AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md`, `.planning/HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md`, `.planning/STATE.md`) can be silently double-updated when multiple background lanes return. Vanilla GSD assumes one orchestrator writer; the harness-improvement program has more independent lanes touching these surfaces.
  - [d:r:i] Background `manager` Task agents running while an operator hand-edits `.planning/` doctrine can miss doctrine updates the reviewer should have read.
  - [d:r:i] Parallel reviewer lanes that merge into consensus synthesis lose adversarial review power. The `Review Consumer Contract` layer guards against this for plan review, not for general audit reviews.
  - [d:r:i] Refmap/topology rewrites (`tooling/codex/audit_refmap.py move` / `retire`) while any lane reads a frozen basis invalidate that lane's paths. Listed as a forbidden overlap in `AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md`, but enforcement is by operator memory.
  - [d:r:i] Installer runs (`scripts/setup-portable-gsd.sh`) while any lane treats `.codex/` as frozen truth corrupt that lane's basis. Same enforcement gap.
- [d:r:i] Asymmetry summary vs vanilla GSD:
  - [d:r:i] The modifier broadens overlap governance (companion-carry checklist, timing-estimate recheck, horizon routing) in ways vanilla GSD does not express, which intensifies safe companion-carry overlap.
  - [d:r:i] The modifier sharpens propagation review into a first-class route (`propagation-review.md`, baseline/delta pair, registry v2), which intensifies safe multi-family contract movement.
  - [d:r:i] The modifier pays a per-spawn ceremony cost (launch-truth, model mapping statement, disposition, bounded duration) that thins purely throughput-driven fan-out forms.
  - [d:r:i] The modifier inherits cross-vendor UI asymmetry it has not resolved: interactive parallel lanes degrade more sharply in Codex than in Claude Code because `request_user_input` has no `multiSelect` and Execute-mode strips the prompt entirely.

## Harness-Improvement Program Overlap

- [e:c+r:i] Already governed:
  - [d:r:i] `Bounded Parallelization And Overlap` in [AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md](../../AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md) (lines 77-104) names earned overlap patterns (external-lane overlap with unrelated governance carry; narrower delegated work with parent-thread composition; change-triggered refresh cadence; bounded reread on a frozen slice), forbidden overlaps (editing packet/spec/prompt/basis a live lane is reading; changing governance role surfaces during a live lane; refmap/topology rewrites that invalidate the basis; crossing the Phase 01 rerun boundary while a lane is returning), and the recheck rule tied to timing estimates.
  - [d:r:i] Horizon routing in [HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md) (lines 48-76) lists five carrier classes (`active bounded slice` / `held later` / `seed` / `deferred` / `doctrine / protected seam` / `audit-family memory`) so concurrent findings flow into different carriers instead of colliding on one surface.
  - [d:r:i] Audit lane scaffolding makes parallel audit lanes reproducible without rebuilding packet/spec/prompt logic. Frozen artifacts (propagation registry, canary reports, runtime-visibility snapshots) give lanes a stable readable object.
  - [d:r:i] Audit-canon absorption and subtree-aging vocabulary (`AUDIT-CANON-ABSORPTION-PROTOCOL.md`, `AUDIT-SUBTREE-AGING-AND-GRADUATION.md`) route completed lane output into durable doctrine without letting the lane subtree silently grow into canon.
- [e:c+r:i] Still depends too much on operator memory:
  - [d:r:i] Which governance surfaces are single-writer is not enumerated. The companion-carry checklist implies it but does not name the set.
  - [d:r:i] Which bounded sub-agent patterns are safely delegable is emerging through the uplift-assist packet family (`entry-uplift-audit/packets/06-12`), but no cross-family reference yet consolidates "composition-keeping delegation" versus "composition-leaking delegation".
  - [d:r:i] Cross-vendor lane launches (`.codex` vs `.claude`) have a parity classifier (`intervention-proposals/134`, `135`) but no rule for what it means to run two wrappers in parallel on the same basis.
  - [d:r:i] What counts as "frozen basis frozen enough" for a secondary lane (tag? commit? no governance-surface edits? no refmap move?) is implicit in the forbidden-overlap list.
  - [d:r:i] Recheck cadence relies on operator discipline to inspect the lane rather than manufacture filler work.
  - [d:r:i] `Ownerless Concerns` in the register names `how the harness in action... should map and govern parallelization opportunities beyond execution-wave splitting`, explicitly flagging that the in-action map is not yet carried.

## Safe Earned Parallelization

- [d:r:i] Wave-based plan execution when the intra-wave `files_modified` overlap detector returns no intersection and the post-merge test gate is active.
- [d:r:i] Four-way codebase mapping with direct-write-to-disk and confirmation-only return (disjoint focus areas: tech / architecture / quality / concerns).
- [d:r:i] New-project parallel researcher sessions with synthesizer-owned composition.
- [d:r:i] One `gsd-doc-classifier` per ingested planning doc in a single multi-Task message, with sequential fallback for runtimes where subagent completion is unreliable.
- [d:r:i] One `gsd-debugger` per UAT gap on a frozen symptom set and frozen implementation basis.
- [d:r:i] Long-running external reviewer lane plus bounded governance carry on an unrelated audit family (change-triggered refreshes, subtree-status updates, launch-ledger housekeeping, register updates).
- [d:r:i] Bounded reread lane on a frozen landed slice while adjacent unrelated families continue.
- [d:r:i] Detect-only specialist carry (`propagation-review` read-only, `uplift-project` detect-only, `seed-migration-inventory` detect-only) during another active lane, provided none of them writes to the governance surfaces the other lane is reading.
- [d:r:i] `manager`-backed background plan/execute Task agents with inline discuss on the operator terminal, provided each background lane stays inside its phase's files and the operator does not hand-edit `.planning/` doctrine mid-run.

## Promising But Not-Yet-Governed Parallelization

- [d:r:i] Pre-execution research split: decompose `gsd-phase-researcher` into parallel disjoint sub-questions (domain / integrations / pitfalls / validation) on a frozen CONTEXT.md, with parent synthesis into `RESEARCH.md`. Earned only when top-level framing is coherent and sub-questions are genuinely separable. Needs a small packet template equivalent to the one `map-codebase` already uses.
- [d:r:i] Post-implementation review family wave: `code-review`, `secure-phase`, `validate-phase`, `ui-review`, `eval-review`, docs-verifier can fan out on a frozen implementation basis. Each already has its own subject and output carrier. Today they run one command at a time; a bounded "review wave" surface would name the disjoint-output invariant and collect returns through one disposition pass.
- [d:r:i] Cross-AI plan review concurrency: today `review.md` forces sequential because of rate limits, but per-CLI run-homes already exist (`$RUN_HOME/raw/{gemini,claude,codex,coderabbit,opencode}.*`) and rate limits are per-key. A guarded async-parallel variant with per-CLI back-off and the existing synthesis step would preserve adversarial rigor while cutting wall-clock without changing the sequential default.
- [d:r:i] Harness-improvement sub-agent delegation patterns (`packet_assembly`, `classification`, `carrier_gap_identification`, `docs_governance_classification`, `cross_runtime_comparison`): the first three patterns are now exercised (`entry-uplift-audit/packets/06-12`). Running two or more of them in the same tranche on disjoint packet inputs is still operator-memory-governed; a compact reference consolidating "what keeps composition" would remove that dependence.
- [d:r:i] Change-triggered refresh fan-out: when one slice triggers refreshes across several propagation-family rows, the registry v2 layered carriers (`propagation-audit/artifacts/02-06`) can be updated in parallel because the layered shape partitions writes. Not yet named as an earned pattern.
- [d:r:i] Cross-vendor parity audits: run `.codex` and `.claude` parity-classifier passes on the same basis from different lanes. Safe today because `.codex` is observed basis and `.claude` is held annotation; governance for when that holds and when it breaks is not yet explicit.
- [d:r:i] Audit-subtree aging sweeps: several subtrees can be aged / graduated in one tranche on the same repo state because each has its own README status line. Currently done one-at-a-time on operator initiative.

## Likely Coherence And Quality Risks

- [d:r:i] Two `gsd-planner` lanes on the same phase basis without a compaction rule: outputs diverge, one has to be re-read or thrown out. Degrades continuity.
- [d:r:i] `discuss-phase` running while the phase's `CONTEXT.md` is being human-edited: interactive prompt adoption races and the steering brief silently drifts.
- [d:r:i] Parallel writes to single-writer governance surfaces (`CURRENT-STATE.md`, `STATUS.md`, `INDEX.md`, `AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md`, `HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md`, `.planning/STATE.md`). Vanilla GSD assumes one orchestrator writer; concurrent audit lanes can both update these and lose the later write.
- [d:r:i] `map-codebase` refresh while `execute-phase` is modifying code: the map is stale the moment it commits.
- [d:r:i] Parallel reviewer fan-out that collapses into consensus synthesis without the `Review Consumer Contract` layer: loses lone high-signal criticism and merely-adequate detection that the repo's anti-threshold doctrine specifically protects.
- [d:r:i] Refmap/topology rewrites (`audit_refmap.py move` / `retire`) while any lane reads a frozen basis: invalidates the lane's paths.
- [d:r:i] Installer runs (`setup-portable-gsd.sh`) while any lane treats `.codex/` as frozen truth: the basis moves under the lane.
- [d:r:i] Crossing the Phase 01 rerun boundary while a lane is still returning on the prior governed baseline: an explicit forbidden overlap in the pattern library and a repeated anti-misread in the governing docs.
- [d:r:i] Background `manager` agents plus concurrent hand-edits of `AGENTS.md`, wrappers, or `.planning/AGENTS.md`: the background agent reads the prior instruction set and acts on stale doctrine.
- [d:r:i] Audit-subtree aging and canon-absorption running in the same tranche that touches the subtrees they classify: the classification output and the subtree state drift.

## Governance And Operator Surface Changes

- [d:r:i] Name single-writer surfaces explicitly. The right carrier is [AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md](../../AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md) `Bounded Parallelization And Overlap`, extended with a `Single-Writer Governance Surfaces` subsection enumerating: `CURRENT-STATE.md`, `STATUS.md`, `INDEX.md`, `AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md`, `HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md`, `.planning/STATE.md`, `.planning/ROADMAP.md`, and `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md`. Later concurrent lanes must route writes through the active-bounded-slice owner rather than the secondary lane.
- [d:r:i] Promote `Ownerless Concerns -> how the harness in action... should map and govern parallelization opportunities` in [HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/HARNESS-IMPROVEMENT-REGISTER.md) into a named Active Improvement Family (`Parallelization field map and overlap governance`) carrying this output as its first slice. The family should point at `AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md` as the current doctrine carrier and at `parallelization-audit/` as the audit-family memory.
- [d:r:i] Add a compact `Fan-Out Packet` template in a later bounded slice (under `intervention-proposals/`) that preserves the top-level-orchestration rule: one packet, N spawns on disjoint inputs, parent-thread composition disposition. Keep it as a reusable carrier, not inline `AGENTS.md` text.
- [d:r:i] Extend [.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/propagation-review.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/propagation-review.md) output shape with an optional `Parallelization Impact` section when the triggering slice changes a parallelization-adjacent surface (`execute-phase.md`, `review.md`, `map-codebase.md`, `ingest-docs.md`, `diagnose-issues.md`, `manager.md`, agent-skills matrix, `config.json.parallelization`). This keeps later changes routing through the same propagation family rather than drive-by edits.
- [d:r:i] Add one doctrine line in [.planning/AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/AGENTS.md) naming what makes a frozen basis frozen enough for a secondary lane: explicit commit or tag; no pending governance-surface edits; no refmap move in flight; no installer reinstall in flight; no active Phase 01 rerun touching. Keep it as one layer, not a new master frame.
- [d:r:i] Do not rewrite live workflows in this slice. `execute-phase.md`, `review.md`, `map-codebase.md`, `ingest-docs.md`, `diagnose-issues.md`, `manager.md` stay out of scope; change them only when a later bounded proposal explicitly earns the move.
- [d:r:i] Do not promote horizon routing into `.planning/AGENTS.md` in this slice. - [d:r:i] This proposal reopens the `project_uplift.py` payload-home judgment after the third neutralization tranche.

## Judgment Questions

### 1. What Still Materially Binds The Helper To This Host?

- [d:r:i] Judge which remaining surfaces still count as host/shared-boundary rather than modifier-owned payload.
- [d:r:i] Make the answer explicit instead of letting the old pre-neutralization intuition continue by inertia.

- [d:r:i] Distinguish:
  - portable modifier payload
  - stable compatibility shim boundary
  - still-shared install/materialization boundary
- [d:r:i] Do not treat all current imports or neighboring references as equal movement pressure.

### 3. What Must Stay Out Of Scope For This Judgment?

- [d:r:i] No relocation implementation in this slice.
- [d:r:i] No `OVERLAY_MANIFEST_REL_PATH` neutralization in this slice.
- [d:r:i] No second overlay tranche in this slice.
- [d:r:i] No overwrite-family source-indirection widening in this slice.
- [d:r:i] No standalone repo or npm/`npx` distribution execution in this slice.

Date: 2026-04-22
Status: frozen external-lane return

# Harness Modifier Development Program Plan Audit

## Overall Judgment

- [g:r:i] Disposition: `accept with revisions`. `166` is the right shape for the next integrated bounded object in the harness-modifier development program. It gathers responsible closure, development-side parallelization, intervention lifecycle discipline, horizons, task-type routing, and actual/virtual intervention surfaces into one carrier without collapsing them, and it keeps deployment-readiness and harness-in-action workflow rewrites out of frame.
- [g:r:i] The revisions are bounded and carry-focused, not a rewrite. The plan's weakest axis is not its structure; it is that it does not yet inherit by name the durable taxonomies already frozen in adjacent lane `01` returns (six-surface split, five-family signal taxonomy, three-class parallelization taxonomy). Without that named inheritance, later consumers will reconstruct those distinctions ad hoc from chat memory or from route note `161` alone, which is exactly what closure lane `01` was trying to prevent.
- [d:r:i] Anti-misread fences the plan must keep (and this audit must keep):
  - [d:r:i] do not let `accept with revisions` collapse into a ship-gate verdict; the plan is a protocol-pressure carrier, not a deployment object
  - [d:r:i] do not let the revisions list become a single implementation queue; they are per-carrier sharpenings with their own ownership
  - [d:r:i] do not demand harness-in-action workflow rewrites from this plan; those stay protected-future carries with their own triggering basis
  - [d:r:i] do not flatten actual and possible intervention surfaces into one inventory; their distinct treatment is part of why `166` is the right next object

## What The Plan Clarifies Well

- [d:r:i] The domain split is load-bearing and correctly named. `166` routes uplift through the six targets (`harness-contract` / `host-artifact` / `harness-agential` / `harness-operational` / `harness-adaptive` / `distribution/deployability`) rather than one overloaded `uplift` umbrella. This preserves the `162` semantic split as the operating vocabulary instead of re-flattening it.
- [d:r:i] The parallelization scope rule is crisp. `Development-side parallelization for the harness-modifier program is the active protocol question now` paired with `Harness-in-action parallelization remains a real later family, but it is not the current implementation target for this plan` closes the main flattening risk that `164` and `165` left open. The `Out of scope for this plan` list in `Parallelization Rule` (harness-in-action workflow rewrites, execute-family/review-family redesigns, broad multi-provider portability) makes the out-of-scope surface a first-class element of the plan rather than an aside.
- [d:r:i] The actual/virtual intervention-surface split is preserved as two distinct sections with different stances. The plan does not treat virtual surfaces as latent implementation debt; it treats them as openable surfaces whose promotion is conditional. That matches the anti-threshold posture from repo doctrine and the protected-futures discipline from `163`.
- [d:r:i] Responsible closure is kept as layered carry, not a finish line. The `Responsible Closure Rule` names the closure question as stronger control / routing / maintainability / adaptive capacity rather than `more proof that the current modifier can run`, and the `Role` section explicitly refuses the ship-gate frame. This is the correct inheritance of lane `01`'s anti-threshold fence.
- [d:r:i] The four-workstream shape (A: dev operations and protocol; B: responsible closure and deployability; C: propagation and verification; D: intervention-surface expansion) partitions ownership cleanly and keeps the current-status line per stream honest (`under-carried`, `first field map completed`, `field map exists but parallelization-adjacent consequences uneven`, `actual partly visible, virtual not yet governed strongly`). The `next type` field on each workstream travels the task-type vocabulary into ownership, which is the right integration move.
- [d:r:i] The `Exact Next Moves` ordering — audit this plan cross-vendor before cutting the next protocol tranche; pair protocol slice with targeted propagation audit on already-landed parallelization-adjacent workflow changes; keep harness-in-action parallelization explicit-but-later — preserves the parallelization internal cross-audit's protocol-pressure recommendation and the closure lane `01`'s pre-deployment sequencing.

## Actual Intervention Surfaces

- [d:r:i] The class-level enumeration in `166` covers the right families: audit/review lane machinery, governance routing, propagation carry, verification and materialization, extraction/rehome work, responsible-closure field mapping, development-overlap governance. Reading it as a map of where intervention is live, the families are partitioned and none is secretly absorbed into another.
- [d:r:i] The weaker axis here is pointer-level. A consumer re-entering the plan has to reconstruct which concrete carriers are meant. The plan would broaden by naming, under each family, at least one current authoritative pointer so the map is usable without a parallel grep pass:
  - [d:r:i] `audit / review lane machinery`: [AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/audits/2026-04-18-readiness-rerun-debrief-and-redesign/AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md), [AUDIT-CANON-ABSORPTION-PROTOCOL.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/audits/2026-04-18-readiness-rerun-debrief-and-redesign/AUDIT-CANON-ABSORPTION-PROTOCOL.md), [AUDIT-SUBTREE-AGING-AND-GRADUATION.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/audits/2026-04-18-readiness-rerun-debrief-and-redesign/AUDIT-SUBTREE-AGING-AND-GRADUATION.md), [AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/audits/2026-04-18-readiness-rerun-debrief-and-redesign/AUDIT-SUBTREE-STATUS-REGISTER.md), and the `capture_launch_truth.py --since` launch-truth carrier
  - [d:r:i] `verification and materialization`: [harness_modifier/contract/harness_canary.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/contract/harness_canary.py), [harness_modifier/contract/runtime_visibility.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/contract/runtime_visibility.py), [harness_modifier/contract/portable_gsd_contract.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/contract/portable_gsd_contract.py), [harness_modifier/contract/manifest_install_coherence.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/contract/manifest_install_coherence.py) where present, and the `verify-materialized --strict` entry
  - [d:r:i] `propagation carry`: [.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/propagation-review.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/propagation-review.md), the `propagation-audit/artifacts/02-06` registry v2 layered carriers, and the baseline/delta pair from `95`/`96`
  - [d:r:i] `extraction / rehome work`: [harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.json](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.json), [harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.py](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/compatibility/declaration.py), [harness_modifier/overlay/helpers/AUTHORITY-MAP.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/overlay/helpers/AUTHORITY-MAP.md), [harness_modifier/overlay/ROSTER.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/harness_modifier/overlay/ROSTER.md), the first overlay source-authority split from `148`, and the host-planning-shape externalization from `159`
  - [d:r:i] `governance routing`: the register's `Horizon Routing` section as the carrier-class surface, not only the register as a whole; [.planning/AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/AGENTS.md) `Launch-Truth Discipline` and `Contract-Propagation Hygiene`; [AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/AGENTS.md) `Delegation And Orchestration`
  - [d:r:i] `development-overlap governance`: [AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/audits/2026-04-18-readiness-rerun-debrief-and-redesign/AUDIT-LANE-PATTERN-LIBRARY.md) `Bounded Parallelization And Overlap` (lines 77-104), with the already-enumerated forbidden-overlap set (governance-role edits, refmap/topology rewrite, installer reinstall, Phase 01 rerun crossing) carried by reference rather than restated
- [d:r:i] One actual surface that is underrepresented: review-workflow carry. The `gsd-review` helper-backed first slice is now landed through `145` plus propagation refresh `53`, and `review-route-audit/` lane `01` is the first completed review-route audit family. `166` currently mentions audit/review lane machinery for harness-improvement-program audits but does not name the review-workflow family as an active intervention surface for the program. It should be added, because later responsible-closure audits and cross-vendor lane launches route through that family.
- [d:r:i] One actual surface that is correctly held at low profile but underpriced: the operator-directive surface in the harness register (`Current Operator Directive`). This is the live steering carrier that tells later lanes what the program is not allowed to shortcut. `166` inherits its spirit (no shortcuts that trade away future control) but does not name it. Naming it turns the directive into one of the plan's own inheritance hooks rather than ambient background.

## Possible Or Virtual Intervention Surfaces

- [d:r:i] The list of nine virtual surfaces in `166` is the right shape for a `virtual`-stance section: development parallelization protocol carrier, intervention lifecycle protocol carrier, single-writer / lane-exclusive authority surface map, fan-out packet template, parallelization impact carrier inside propagation-review, development intervention-surface map, measurement/provenance carrier, observation carrier for host exercises, dogfooding surface.
- [d:r:i] Three of these are not `virtual` in the sense `166` currently uses; they are already classified as `held-later` carries under `parallelization-audit/` lane `01`'s disposition:
  - [d:r:i] `fan-out packet template` — held-later per [parallelization-audit/dispositions/01](../../parallelization-audit/dispositions/01-harness-parallelization-field-map-and-diagnosis-audit-inheritance.md) `Keep Explicitly Later`, with the triggering basis named (`after one more real overlap exercise`)
  - [d:r:i] `single-writer / lane-exclusive authority surface map` — held-later per the same disposition, with the triggering basis named (`verify it against one real multi-lane tranche before treating it as binding`)
  - [d:r:i] `parallelization impact carrier inside propagation-review` — held-later per the same disposition, with the triggering basis named (`when a bounded proposal next touches a parallelization-adjacent surface`)
- [d:r:i] Re-listing these three as `virtual` without naming their prior `held-later` carry risks silently demoting them. The plan broadens by distinguishing two sub-classes inside the section: surfaces that are already `held-later` with a named triggering basis, and surfaces that are net-virtual (no trigger yet earned). The other six entries stay net-virtual.
- [d:r:i] The virtual-surface promotion criteria in `166` are AND-joined as if all five were gates (`repeated pressure appears across more than one family; current carriers cannot hold; ownership can be made explicit; propagation consequences can be named; surface can be audited or verified once opened`). That reads as a bar. It should read as maturity indicators, any of which broadens the case for promotion:
  - [d:r:i] pressure replication signal (repeated across families)
  - [d:r:i] carrier insufficiency signal (current carriers fold the distinction rather than hold it)
  - [d:r:i] ownership nameability (someone could own it explicitly)
  - [d:r:i] propagation traceability (consequences can be enumerated in advance)
  - [d:r:i] audit/verification shape (the surface is inspectable once opened)
  - [d:r:i] rule of thumb: two or more signals earn a bounded proposal; all five earn promotion into an active carrier. Keeping this as signals-not-gates preserves the anti-threshold posture the rest of the plan carries.
- [d:r:i] One virtual surface that is shaped more sharply than `166` admits: `observation carrier for host exercises`. Closure lane `01` already specified what this carrier holds in its first slice (five signal families: `deployment-context` / `expectation-vs-observation` / `semantic-deviation` / `positive-gain` / `measurement-provenance`; observe-only; operator-triggered; single-writer; keyed to one host exercise; v2_split-style provenance). `166` should name this inheritance so the first proposal under that surface is not drafted from scratch.
- [d:r:i] One virtual surface the plan does not carry but the closure lane `01` schedule names: the cross-vendor responsible-closure audit from `161` commitment #6. Closure lane `01` explicitly said this should be held-later-scheduled against payload-home closure plus the first observation-carrier slice, not left ambient. `166` should carry it as a sixth `held-later-with-trigger` entry in the virtual/possible list so it does not quietly evaporate.

## Horizon Routing

- [d:r:i] The three-layer stack (short / medium / long) is present and mostly clean, and the `Scope Rule` at the top declares harness-program horizons distinct from host-product horizons. The separation holds at the doctrinal level but thins at each horizon layer. A later reader skimming only `Short Horizon` could re-import `.planning/LONG-ARC.md` or `.planning/ROADMAP.md` as the default long-horizon frame, which is exactly the misread `163` was written to prevent.
- [d:r:i] One broadening move: label each horizon heading with the program it belongs to (`Short Horizon (harness-program)`) so the inheritance from `163` is visible inside the horizon sections, not only inside the `Scope Rule`. The mapping is:
  - [d:r:i] `Short Horizon` → `Near Horizon` in `163` (current bounded slice plus required neighboring carry)
  - [d:r:i] `Medium Horizon` → `Medium Horizon` in `163` (active family field)
  - [d:r:i] `Long Horizon` → `Far Horizon` in `163` (orienting future, protected futures)
- [d:r:i] The `Long Horizon` protected-futures list in `166` carries five of the six protected futures from `163`: standalone repo, npm/npx distribution, dogfooding, richer telemetry/semantic-signal capture, parallelization-in-action. It does not carry `broader host-context deployability` as an explicit protected future, which `163` named. Adding it closes the protection of the `{.codex, .claude, mixed, regular-GSD host, GSD-Reflect-coexistence host}` field without turning it into an implementation promise.
- [d:r:i] One sequencing point the horizon stack could sharpen: the revision grammar from `163` (`when a review or audit materially changes the path, update near-horizon slice and governance carry; revise medium-horizon family routing if the family shape changed; revise far-horizon orientation only if the result actually changes the protected future or extraction/deployability direction`) is the intervention lifecycle discipline in horizon form. `166` currently points lifecycle pressure at a virtual `intervention lifecycle protocol carrier` but does not name `163`'s revision grammar as already-partly-governing that pressure. Naming it turns `163` into inherited doctrine for the lifecycle family rather than background.

## Task-Type Routing

- [d:r:i] All seven task types (exploration / audit / research / planning / implementation / verification / governance) are routed, and each has at least one concrete carrier or target named. The routing is partitioned by stance (exploration opens; audit tests; research gathers; planning proposes; implementation closes; verification confirms; governance preserves), which keeps the task-type surface from collapsing into one `work queue`.
- [d:r:i] Two sharpenings broaden the task-type routing:
  - [d:r:i] `proposal` is absent as a task type. In the harness-improvement program, `intervention-proposals/` is the analog of `discuss-phase` in host-side GSD: it is where the bounded next carrier is shaped before planning. `166` currently hides this under `planning`. Carrying `proposal` as its own row (with `intervention-proposals/` as the carrier) makes the distinction between shaping a bounded next carrier and planning the tranche that executes it visible.
  - [d:r:i] `measurement / observation` is split awkwardly between `verification` (`propagation refresh validation`) and implicit under `governance`. The five-family signal taxonomy from closure lane `01` does not belong to either of those in the way `166` currently routes them; it belongs to a `measurement` task type that the plan does not yet name. Carrying `measurement` as its own row (with the observation carrier and `measurement-provenance` family named) keeps later telemetry work from degrading into verification pass/fail tallies.
- [d:r:i] One task-type carry that `166` implies but does not state: governance-side launch-truth and disposition-verb discipline (`accept` / `revise` / `park` / `reject`) is the lifecycle-discipline form that keeps parallel audit lanes individually auditable. `166` names `launch-truth and ledger upkeep` under `governance` but does not carry the disposition-verb set, which is what closure lane `01` singled out as the harness-operational surface. Adding the disposition-verb set to `governance` closes the gap.

## Parallelization And Lifecycle Protocol Pressure

- [d:r:i] Parallelization is correctly routed as a development-program multiplier, not as a harness-in-action rewrite agenda. The plan names the right overlap patterns for this lane (external plan audit + unrelated governance carry; later paired internal audit + parent-thread plan revision; later targeted propagation audit on already-landed workflow slices alongside bounded read-only audit) and the right out-of-scope set (workflow rewrites, execute/review-family redesigns, broad multi-provider).
- [d:r:i] What the plan does not yet inherit by name: the three-class taxonomy from [parallelization-audit/outputs/01](../../parallelization-audit/outputs/01-harness-parallelization-field-map-and-diagnosis-audit-opus47-max-r1.md):
  - [d:r:i] `safe earned` — fan-out on a frozen basis with disjoint outputs, companion-carry on unrelated governance surfaces, detect-only specialist lanes
  - [d:r:i] `promising but not-yet-governed` — review-family wave, pre-execution research split, cross-vendor parity lane, async-parallel cross-AI review
  - [d:r:i] `likely coherence/quality risk` — parallel writes to single-writer governance surfaces, refmap/topology rewrites during a live lane, installer runs during a live lane, consensus-flattening reviewer fan-out, Phase 01 rerun boundary crossed during a returning lane
- [d:r:i] Naming the three-class taxonomy inside `Parallelization Rule` (as inheritance, not re-derivation) turns `166`'s overlap list into instances of classes that later lanes can also instance against, rather than one-off examples. It also lets the forbidden-overlap set (Phase 01 rerun crossing, refmap rewrites during a live lane, installer reinstalls during a live lane, concurrent writes to single-writer governance surfaces) travel without being restated each time.
- [d:r:i] Lifecycle protocol pressure is present but partly virtual. `166` names `propose -> launch -> monitor -> review -> disposition -> propagate -> verify -> revise` under the virtual `intervention lifecycle protocol carrier`. Three of those stages already have governed carriers the plan does not point at:
  - [d:r:i] `launch` — launch-truth capture per [AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/AGENTS.md) `Delegation And Orchestration`, `capture_launch_truth.py --since`, `launch-truth/` subdirectories
  - [d:r:i] `disposition` — disposition-verb requirement per [AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/AGENTS.md) and the `dispositions/NN-*-inheritance.md` shape
  - [d:r:i] `propagate` — propagation-review route per [.planning/AGENTS.md](/home/rookslog/workspace/projects/prix-guesser/.planning/AGENTS.md) `Contract-Propagation Hygiene` and `.codex/get-shit-done/workflows/propagation-review.md`
- [d:r:i] The virtual carrier should name itself as `lifecycle protocol consolidation`, not `lifecycle protocol creation`. The consolidation task is to join the three already-governed stages with the still-under-carried stages (`monitor`, `review`, `revise`) under one readable surface, not to invent the whole pipeline from scratch. That framing keeps the already-earned carry visible and narrows the consolidation proposal's bounded shape.
- [d:r:i] One lifecycle pressure the plan does not yet name: post-return `revise` discipline. `163`'s revision grammar (near → medium → far revision after audit returns) is the `revise` stage in horizon form. `166` should point the virtual `intervention lifecycle protocol carrier` at `163`'s revision rules as partial existing carry so the later consolidation proposal does not silently rewrite horizon doctrine.

## Responsible Closure Sequencing

- [d:r:i] The `Exact Next Moves` ordering is directionally correct:
  1. this plan audited cross-vendor

# Harness Modifier Development Program Plan Audit

## Overall Judgment

- [g:r:i] Disposition: `accept with revisions`. `166` is the right shape for the next integrated bounded object in the harness-modifier development program. It gathers responsible closure, development-side parallelization, intervention lifecycle discipline, horizons, task-type routing, and actual/virtual intervention surfaces into one carrier without collapsing them, and it keeps deployment-readiness and harness-in-action workflow rewrites out of frame.
- [g:r:i] The revisions are bounded and carry-focused, not a rewrite. The plan's weakest axis is not its structure; it is that it does not yet inherit by name the durable taxonomies already frozen in adjacent lane `01` returns (six-surface split, five-family signal taxonomy, three-class parallelization taxonomy). Without that named inheritance, later consumers will reconstruct those distinctions ad hoc from chat memory or from route note `161` alone, which is exactly what closure lane `01` was trying to prevent.
- [d:r:i] Anti-misread fences the plan must keep (and this audit must keep):
  - [d:r:i] do not let `accept with revisions` collapse into a ship-gate verdict; the plan is a protocol-pressure carrier, not a deployment object
  - [d:r:i] do not let the revisions list become a single implementation queue; they are per-carrier sharpenings with their own ownership
  - [d:r:i] do not demand harness-in-action workflow rewrites from this plan; those stay protected-future carries with their own triggering basis
  - [d:r:i] do not flatten actual and possible intervention surfaces into one inventory; their distinct treatment is part of why `166` is the right next object

## What The Plan Clarifies Well

- [d:r:i] The domain split is load-bearing and correctly named. `166` routes uplift through the six targets (`harness-contract` / `host-artifact` / `harness-agential` / `harness-operational` / `harness-adaptive` / `distribution/deployability`) rather than one overloaded `uplift` umbrella. This preserves the `162` semantic split as the operating vocabulary instead of re-flattening it.
- [d:r:i] The parallelization scope rule is crisp. `Development-side parallelization for the harness-modifier program is the active protocol question now` paired with `Harness-in-action parallelization remains a real later family, but it is not the current implementation target for this plan` closes the main flattening risk that `164` and `165` left open. The `Out of scope for this plan` list in `Parallelization Rule` (harness-in-action workflow rewrites, execute-family/review-family redesigns, broad multi-provider portability) makes the out-of-scope surface a first-class element of the plan rather than an aside.
- [d:r:i] The actual/virtual intervention-surface split is preserved as two distinct sections with different stances. The plan does not treat virtual surfaces as latent implementation debt; it treats them as openable surfaces whose promotion is conditional. That matches the anti-threshold posture from repo doctrine and the protected-futures discipline from `163`.
- [d:r:i] Responsible closure is kept as layered carry, not a finish line. The `Responsible Closure Rule` names the closure question as stronger control / routing / maintainability / adaptive capacity rather than `more proof that the current modifier can run`, and the `Role` section explicitly refuses the ship-gate frame. This is the correct inheritance of lane `01`'s anti-threshold fence.
- [d:r:i] The four-workstream shape (A: dev operations and protocol; B: responsible closure and deployability; C: propagation and verification; D: intervention-surface expansion) partitions ownership cleanly and keeps the current-status line per stream honest (`under-carried`, `first field map completed`, `field map exists but parallelization-adjacent consequences uneven`, `actual partly visible, virtual not yet governed strongly`). The `next type` field on each workstream travels the task-type vocabulary into ownership, which is the right integration move.
- [d:r:i] The `Exact Next Moves` ordering — audit this plan cross-vendor before cutting the next protocol tranche; pair protocol slice with targeted propagation audit on already-landed parallelization-adjacent workflow changes; keep harness-in-action parallelization explicit-but-later — preserves the parallelization internal cross-audit's protocol-pressure recommendation and the closure lane `01`'s pre-deployment sequencing.

## Actual Intervention Surfaces

- [d:r:i] The class-level enumeration in `166` covers the right families: audit/review lane machinery, governance routing, propagation carry, verification and materialization, extraction/rehome work, responsible-closure field mapping, development-overlap governance. - [d:r:i] One actual surface that is underrepresented: review-workflow carry. The `gsd-review` helper-backed first slice is now landed through `145` plus propagation refresh `53`, and `review-route-audit/` lane `01` is the first completed review-route audit family. `166` currently mentions audit/review lane machinery for harness-improvement-program audits but does not name the review-workflow family as an active intervention surface for the program. ## Possible Or Virtual Intervention Surfaces

# Harness Modifier Development Program Plan Audit

## Overall Judgment

- [g:r:i] Disposition: `accept with revisions`. `166` is the right shape for the next integrated bounded object in the harness-modifier development program. It gathers responsible closure, development-side parallelization, intervention lifecycle discipline, horizons, task-type routing, and actual/virtual intervention surfaces into one carrier without collapsing them, and it keeps deployment-readiness and harness-in-action workflow rewrites out of frame.

Without that named inheritance, later consumers will reconstruct those distinctions ad hoc from chat memory or from route note `161` alone, which is exactly what closure lane `01` was trying to prevent.

## What The Plan Clarifies Well
